papers.abstract: Subset size determines the balance between robustness and efficiency in minimum covariance determinant estimation. Conventional choices fix this balance before the extent and structure of contamination are known. Reweighting does not remove the influence of the initial subset size. We propose a data-adaptive rule based on ordered squared Mahalanobis distances. It selects the first window maximum, with window width proportional to the sample size. For a minimum covariance determinant subset, the statistic equals the smallest squared distance among excluded observations. For smooth elliptical distributions with small one-point contamination, we characterize the first population window maximum. Under suitable conditions, it is the last retained fraction at which excluding the contaminating point remains optimal. We derive a first-order expansion for this boundary and establish sample localization along the full integer path. Without contamination, the selected fraction tends to one. A fast depth-based implementation reuses one ordering across candidate sizes. Simulations under Gaussian and heavy-tailed sampling show gains over fixed subset sizes, most consistently for scatter estimation. Real data analyses show that the initial subset size affects which observations are retained after reweighting.

papers.title: Beam-beam effects on measurements at electron-positron colliders: LEP neutrino counting and Higgs factories
papers.authors: Brendon Madison
papers.abstract: Beam-beam electromagnetic interactions affect the luminosity, collision energy, polarization, and particle backgrounds relevant to precision measurements at electron-positron colliders. We investigate these effects using Fast $e^{\pm}e^{\pm}$ Beam and Luminosity (FeeBL), a new beam-beam simulation framework, and compare its predictions with published results from LEP and proposed future colliders. We reproduce the analytical field-integration calculations of LEP Bhabha scattering and identify an approximately 2% bias in previously published beam-deflection simulations. Applying the corresponding luminosity correction and a revised uncertainty assessment motivated by the observed agreement among the four LEP experiments yields ($N_ν= 2.9965 \pm 0.0040$), compared with the previously reported ($2.9963 \pm 0.0074$). The revised uncertainty is conditional on an assumed common rescaling of experiment specific uncertainties and motivates further investigation of the original uncertainty budgets. We identify and correct implementation errors in the modeling of Breit-Wheeler, Bethe-Heitler, and Landau-Lifshitz pair production, with implications for detector backgrounds at Higgs factories. Simulated beam depolarization and luminosity spectra are compared with existing ILC and HALHF predictions. Finally, we investigate collision energy monochromatization for direct Higgs production, obtaining sub-MeV collision energy peak widths in exploratory linear collider configurations at substantial luminosity cost, while finding significantly weaker narrowing for the FCC-ee configurations studied. We derive a rigid Gaussian beam overlap model and estimate that FCC-ee needs roughly 10 m of horizontal only dispersion to reach widths of $\approx1~\mathrm{MeV}$.

papers.title: Variational free complement method with Gaussian expanded complement functions: extensions of general atomic framework including helium and lithium ground states with geminal induced expansion length
papers.authors: Cong Wang
papers.abstract: We expand the previous framework of hierarchical-decontraction Gaussian expanded complement functions approach (arXiv: 2603.16262v2) of the free complement (FC) method to $N$-electron atomic systems including general permutations. We consider the possibility that the Gaussian expansion length depends on the presence of the geminal $g$ function. To be more specific, fewer expansion length shall be used when the two-electron $g$ function is combined with the initial wavefunction. The present approach is applied to the ground states of the helium and lithium atoms. The complement function generations via 2s$\rightarrow$1s channel in the lithium ground state are discussed. Symmetries for the associated $N$-electron integrals are analyzed.

papers.title: A forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models: an EFM3D case study for crime scene reconstruction
papers.authors: Davidson Chisom Onwubiko; Shahana Bano; Carlos Francisco Moreno-García
papers.abstract: Foundation models increasingly combine geometry, semantics, and spatial context for three-dimensional scene understanding, but their suitability for forensic crime scene reconstruction remains unclear. This study presents a structured forensic evaluation framework for egocentric foundation models and demonstrates it using the Egocentric Foundation Model for 3D (EFM3D). Four simulated indoor crime scenes were recorded with Meta Project Aria Gen~1 at Robert Gordon University's East Lodge House forensic training facility. The framework evaluates room-scale reconstruction, semantic scene understanding, computational performance, and forensic suitability. Across the four scenes, EFM3D generated meshes averaging $12{,}668\pm2{,}430$ vertices and $24{,}838\pm4{,}903$ faces, with 39,529 recorded semantic predictions spanning 21--24 categories at a mean confidence of 0.40. Because reference meshes and expert-labelled 3D ground truth were unavailable, these statistics are treated as descriptive outputs rather than measures of geometric or detection accuracy. Final inference runs processed $1{,}388\pm203$ snippets per scene at $0.69\pm0.01$ samples/s and required $50.77\pm6.12$ minutes per recording. A seven-criterion capability profile indicated stronger support for room geometry, furniture localisation, scene context, and spatial relationships than for fine-scale forensic evidence. The results position EFM3D as a complementary tool for contextual documentation and scene review rather than a replacement for high-fidelity forensic capture. The framework provides a reproducible basis for evaluating future egocentric foundation models in specialised forensic settings.

papers.title: A Game-Theoretic MPC Planner for Cooperative and Adversarial Drone Coordination
papers.authors: Zdeněk Bouček; Miroslav Flídr
papers.abstract: We present and evaluate a game-theoretic model predictive control planner for cooperative goal reaching and adversarial pursuit-evasion with drones. The planner combines 3D prediction, individual objectives, optional shared separation constraints and trajectory-tracking interfaces. A comparison of cooperative game solvers assesses their ability to find feasible trajectories that resolve conflicts. A computational study quantifies how number of drones, prediction horizon and move blocking affect computation time and numerical acceptance. Move blocking holds control inputs constant over groups of prediction steps, reducing the number of independent control variables and lowering computation time. Timing measurements identify the practical limits of real-time planning in the tested configurations. PyBullet simulations demonstrate cooperative goal reaching and pursuit-evasion. A laboratory flight complements the simulations by validating the trajectory-tracking interfaces on physical drones. The planner can serve as a basis for further evaluation and controller development.

papers.title: Spectral-Domain Information Geometry of Stationary Covariance Models: Gaussian and Elliptical Extensions
papers.authors: Shu Yang; Dongying Li; Wenxian Yu
papers.abstract: This paper develops an information-geometric framework for stationary covariance structures. We begin with the infinite-dimensional setting, where stationary covariance structures can be characterized without finite-window boundary effects. By formulating the covariance structure as a bilinear form on a suitable class of test functions, we establish its spectral representation and show how finite-dimensional Toeplitz covariance matrices arise as restrictions to nested observation subspaces. For zero-mean proper complex Gaussian wide-sense stationary (WSS) processes, we show that the normalized finite-dimensional Fisher information converges to a spectral-domain metric. In logarithmic spectral coordinates, this metric becomes the standard $L^2$ inner product, yielding an explicit Fisher--Rao distance that is also recovered as the asymptotic normalized affine-invariant Riemannian distance between Toeplitz covariance matrices.   We then extend the framework to elliptical observation models by separating global covariance scale from shape. The shape Fisher information is orthogonal to radial nuisance directions and is characterized by a dimension- and radial-model-dependent coefficient. We derive a condition under which this coefficient converges to its Gaussian value as the observation dimension tends to infinity. The resulting limiting spectral-shape geometry is the centered $L^2$ geometry of log-spectra and is invariant to positive rescaling. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical convergence results and the recovery of the Gaussian shape coefficient.

papers.title: Good Views Are Not Enough: Global Counterexamples for Gaussian-Regularized JEPAs
papers.authors: Anran Xu
papers.abstract: Good views do not suffice to guarantee scene invariance or uniqueness up to rotation at the global optima of Gaussian-regularized JEPAs. We give globally certified counterexamples showing that the uniqueness premise of the Gaussian extension in Good Views fails for specified soft objectives. Gaussian marginal matching can reward retaining independently resampled observation variation, and this benefit can exceed its prediction cost. In a four-state model, comparison against the entire scene-only class proves that every global minimizer splits a scene and admits an equal-value partner outside its rotation orbit. In a 512-dimensional model with a complete scene basis, a spectral gap, and exact population whitening, pooled Epps-Pulley regularization still forces every global minimizer to retain nuisance and yields positive cross-modal alignment error even after the best rotation when modality nuisances are independent. Better scene alignment can also accompany worse prediction. With matched 512-label readout budgets and 1% observation noise, whitened prediction JEPA aligns better to the scene than next-token prediction but incurs 0.2872 nats/token higher linear-readout test NLL. A Bayes-risk decomposition distinguishes information lost through the observation channel from the fitted readout's difficulty using retained information. These results connect three determinants of learned representations: what views share, what regularization favors, and what a prediction task can use.

papers.title: Particle Swarm Optimization Strategies for Lensed Gravitational Waves: Parameter Estimation, Source Classification, and Accelerated Sampling
papers.authors: Weiqing Yu; Meng Zhang; Xiaobo Zou; Xiao Guo
papers.abstract: The detection and parameter estimation of lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals are crucial for astrophysics and cosmology. Strong lensing introduces extra parameters, rendering the search high-dimensional, multi-modal, and strongly nonlinear. We apply Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to the search, parameter estimation, and classification of lensed compact binary coalescence GWs within a four-detector coherent network. Using the restricted 2-PN waveform as a template and a model-independent double-image lens parameterization, we assess PSO on both model-matched 2-PN signals and template-mismatched IMRPhenomD signals. Results show effective recovery of chirp mass, mass ratio, sky location, and lens parameters in the 2-PN case, with mass biases appearing under waveform mismatch. A three-class classification pipeline combining 12 PSO runs, majority voting, and a flux ratio threshold achieves 86.19% accuracy in distinguishing lensed GWs, unlensed GWs, and noise. We further propose PSO_GAUSS_MIX method, which constructs a Gaussian mixture prior from PSO estimates for nested sampling, yielding speedups of 1.38x in the restricted 2-PN cases while preserving posterior accuracy. These results establish PSO as an efficient optimizer for lensed GW searches and an effective prior constructor for Bayesian parameter estimation.

papers.title: Spatial effects of Kuramoto modeling on the power-grid frequencies
papers.authors: Kristóf Benedek; Michelle T. Cirunay; Sangita Dutta; Attila Balogh; Bálint Hartmann et al.
papers.abstract: Spatial coupling and heterogeneity can generate complex power-grid frequency dynamics. We investigate the contributions of spatial structure, intrinsic nonlinear dynamics, and external driving using the Kuramoto model (KM), with and without uncorrelated noise, and compare its predictions with real-grid measurements.   We analyse one month of 100 ms frequency measurements from 16 Hungarian transmission-grid sites and simulate the KM on a 387-node transmission network and two-dimensional lattices. The measured power spectra exhibit two scaling regimes, with exponents of approximately 1.63 and 2.23. One-second frequency increments decorrelate rapidly, while correlations of their local inverse variance decay slowly, initially as a power law, $τ^{-0.26(2)}$, up to 15 minutes. A superstatistical Gaussian mixture based on measured local variances captures much of the non-Gaussian increment distribution, but not the rare extreme events.   We also estimate the non-stationary long-time frequency autocorrelation exponent. KM simulations on low-dimensional networks exhibit algebraically decaying autocorrelations and power spectra, consistent with the measurements and the Wiener-Khinchin relation in the steady state. On the heterogeneous transmission network, partial synchronization and frequency locking produce persistent spatial patterns and multi-peaked frequency distributions. However, neither deterministic KM dynamics nor independent Gaussian driving reproduces the measured spectra and increment statistics simultaneously. Moreover, empirical frequency fluctuations are largely shared across substations, whereas simulated fluctuations mainly reflect relative node motion. These findings suggest that spatially coupled nonlinear dynamics contribute to observed frequency fluctuations alongside external driving, including 15-minute power dispatches.

papers.title: RAPA: Ray-Aware Physics Augmentation for Robust Camera-LiDAR Calibration
papers.authors: Kyung-Rin Oh; Ji-Hoon Kim; TaeJoon Ha; Jae-Sang Hyun
papers.abstract: Camera-LiDAR calibration is essential for reliable perception in robotic and autonomous systems. Most target-based calibration methods rely on checkerboard observations, but accurate checkerboard feature extraction from LiDAR point clouds remains challenging due to measurement sparsity. Existing approaches either require manual annotation of 3D corners or depend on geometric feature extraction methods, both of which can become unreliable when checkerboard features are insufficiently observed. In this paper, we formulate checkerboard localization as a 2D detection problem using cylindrical LiDAR reflectivity images. To overcome the limited availability of labeled training data, we propose ray-aware physics augmentation (RAPA), which generates diverse synthetic samples from a single checkerboard observation. The generated data are used to improve detector robustness and generalization under varying sensing conditions. Across four independently captured indoor and outdoor locations, the proposed synthetic augmentation exceeds the strongest evaluated image-space augmentation baseline by 16.1-43.1 percentage points in mAP@0.5. Compared with training-free target-based methods on 242 observations, RAPA yields the largest number of valid target localizations, with 96.4% of its returned detections yielding valid target poses. These reliable localizations support downstream camera-LiDAR calibration across all four evaluated locations. Overall, RAPA addresses a key bottleneck in target-based calibration by enabling automated LiDAR-side target localization with only a single annotated target observation.

papers.title: Topology, geometry and fabrication of volumetric plain weaves
papers.authors: Samuel Poincloux; Lauren Carelli Dreier; Tian Chen
papers.abstract: Plain weave is one of the simplest woven structures, formed by two sets of yarns that cross at right angles in an alternating over-under pattern. While such woven fabrics are usually confined to a 2D surface, here we propose a practical approach to fabricate volumetric plain weaves, entanglements featuring three mutually orthogonal families of yarns threaded through a cubic lattice. We develop an analytic framework that converts the crossing pattern topology into continuous yarn centreline geometries, which we then leverage to fabricate volumetric weave specimens. Each crossing is encoded by a matrix that defines the offsets of the three yarns at a vertex. These are formulated to preserve the plain weave topology in every plane, where each pair of yarn families interlaces as in a planar plain weave. Eight configurations in four opposite pairs exist, yet all are related by rotations and translations, so that the fully alternating volumetric plain weave has a single topology. We adopt sinusoidal yarn trajectories and show that the crossing matrix defines their phases. We select two solutions: in-phase planar zigzags and out-of-phase circular helices. Both are members of a family of elliptical helices that also admits a free choice of handedness for each yarn. We then derive the conditions under which yarns intersect between vertices. In-phase yarns never intersect, whereas helical yarns of equal handedness intersect at a critical offset of $\sqrt{2}λ/16$, with $λ$ the wavelength of the cubic lattice. No assignment of handedness avoids these intersections. Finally, we fabricate volumetric plain weaves by 3D printing and manual assembly from cotton cord. The framework provides a direct basis for generating weave geometries for simulation and fabrication.

papers.title: GTAGym: Real AAA Game Tasks Environment for Evaluation and Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Jiajun Chen; Shicheng Fang; Jiahao Lu; Yuxin Wang; Xipeng Qiu
papers.abstract: AAA games offer a rich testbed for evaluating agent perception, reasoning, and control. However, evaluating whether agents can complete tasks in AAA games is challenging and often human-annotated because task outcomes are often difficult to verify automatically, let alone applying it for Reinforcement Learning (RL). We introduce GTAGym, an environment and framework for evaluation and RL on GTA V tasks. Its evaluation benchmark, GTAVBench, derived from GTA V main-story missions, contains 103 online tasks reconstructed across nine task families, alongside 47 image-based shooting and sniping tasks using GTA V imagery. A web server provides access to the online environment and evaluation interface, supporting parallel testing through screenshots and keyboard-mouse actions with automatic engine-state outcome checks. We evaluate six frontier LLMs on GTAVBench with textual task instructions and on its GTAVBench-AGI branch, where instructions appear only in the first screenshot and a harness automatically compresses interaction history. The best configuration achieves 70.9% overall accuracy in GTAVBench-AGI, yet aerial navigation, evasion and interception remain difficult. GTAGym also provides a scalable generator that samples task parameters within user-specified ranges and option sets under fixed templates, creating batches of 3D and image-based shooting environments for RL with automatic reward and termination signals. LoRA RL of Qwen3.8-27B on generated on-foot navigation tasks improves the in-domain performance and transfers to out-of-domain task categories, and native GTA V tasks from 15% to 23%.

papers.title: Matrix-vector models for the 3D Ising CFT
papers.authors: Kaichi Mizohata; Tatsuya Seko; Asato Tsuchiya
papers.abstract: The construction of three-dimensional conformal field theories (3D CFTs) using interacting fermions in the lowest Landau level on a sphere has recently proven remarkably efficient, while it differs from that of conventional field theories on the fuzzy sphere. Focusing on the 3D Ising CFT, we consider a class of models that are defined by deformed Hamiltonians specified by a function which controls how the interaction is damped at high angular momenta, and this class includes the original model. We show that each model in the class can be reformulated in a basis-independent manner as a matrix--vector quantum-mechanical model, and, upon integrating out the fermionic vectors, as a matrix model. We then focus on a Gaussian choice, for which the bosonic matrices acquire a heat-kernel propagator whose width is controlled by a parameter $ξ$. Through exact diagonalization with the number of fermions up to $16$, we find that the low-energy spectra of the deformed Hamiltonians at criticality agree with those in the 3D Ising CFT for a range of $ξ$. We thus obtain matrix-model realizations of the 3D Ising CFT that, in contrast to conventional fuzzy-sphere field theories, show no sign of UV/IR mixing in the low-lying spectrum.

papers.title: Low-rank Low Precision Training of Gaussian Processes
papers.authors: Moritz Poguntke; Eda Oktay; Yuanzhe Xi; Erin Carson; Martin Stoll
papers.abstract: Training Gaussian processes (GPs) at large scale is computationally challenging because evaluating the log-marginal likelihood and its gradients involves large, dense kernel matrices. We develop a scalable low-rank GP training approach that combines AnchorNet landmark selection with a fully independent training conditional (FITC) correction. The resulting objective and its analytic gradients can be evaluated using low-rank factors, diagonal quantities, and small dense matrices, without forming the full kernel matrix or its derivatives. The complete training procedure is implemented in single precision and evaluated on nine large-scale regression datasets. Across these problems, the method reaches the reference predictive accuracy while substantially reducing training time, although the required approximation rank varies across datasets. We also study the numerical behavior of the full-kernel predictive solve and show that single precision can become limiting for ill-conditioned problems. Finally, we investigate further reducing selected matrix operations to fp16 or TF32. These lower-precision variants provide only modest additional speedups and can become unreliable when the reduced system is poorly conditioned.

papers.title: SAFE-Hair: Scalp-Anchored Fields for Exportable Single-View Hair Reconstruction
papers.authors: Yucheng Wang; Zedong Wang; Yuetong Wu; Yue Ma; Dan Xu
papers.abstract: Single-view 3D hair reconstruction has progressed rapidly, but many methods optimize for visual plausibility rather than producing strand assets that can be directly used in grooming, editing, or simulation pipelines. We propose SAFE-Hair, a framework that reconstructs explicit strand grooms from a single portrait by decoding hair from persistent follicles in a canonical scalp-UV domain. Given a fitted template head, SAFE-Hair projects self-supervised image features onto the scalp, uses a conditional Rectified Flow model to generate latent scalp fields, and decodes occupancy, segment directions, length allocation, and total length at a fixed set of scalp follicles. This representation enforces scalp-rooted strand identities by construction and enables direct export with follicle IDs and guide-family metadata. We further introduce attachment, collision, and bending priors to improve geometric validity without per-subject test-time optimization. To evaluate both reconstruction fidelity and asset usability, we introduce HairBench-3D, a benchmark built from public 3D hair assets with standardized alignment, rendering, resampling, and metrics for geometry, direction consistency, invisible-region completion, silhouette agreement, and collision. SAFE-Hair improves Chamfer distance from 3.74 mm to 3.28 mm, F-score from 77.9 to 81.7, invisible-region F-score from 66.1 to 69.8, and penetration ratio from 4.8% to 3.9% over the strongest baseline.

papers.title: Scale-Invariant Empirical-Bayes Laplace Approximation for ReLU Networks
papers.authors: Shivam Pal; Piyush Rai
papers.abstract: ReLU networks are well-known to have continuous scale symmetries; infinitely many reparameterized weight vectors that represent the same function. Dinh et al. (2017) have shown that, by reparameterizing, the geometry of the loss landscape (e.g., curvature) of these networks can be changed arbitrarily without affecting the underlying function. Thus, any quantity that depends on the network's geometry should be defined with care. In this paper, we show that the Empirical Bayes (EB) Laplace's approximation is not well-defined for ReLU networks, mainly due to Hessian dependence in computing the marginal likelihood, which is not invariant under ReLU scale symmetries. Thus, we can get different prior precisions, posterior covariances, and predictive uncertainties for a network having identical predictions under ReLU scaling. We define family of prior precision fields indexed by $γ$ and introduce $γ$-canonicalization, which first converts the network to its canonical representation by balancing the ratio of incoming to outgoing weights, and then fits the Empirical Bayes (EB) Laplace to the canonical representation. This procedure is equivalent to transporting the isotropic Gaussian prior from the canonical representation to the original coordinates, by producing a ReLU-scale-compatible precision field. This makes the marginal likelihood invariant under ReLU scaling, while allowing $γ$ to be selected by maximizing the marginal likelihood. The resulting EB Laplace approximation is well-defined on ReLU scale-equivalence classes and yields consistent prior precision selection and predictive uncertainties across functionally identical parameterizations.

papers.title: Parametric spatio-temporal reduced-order modelling via Spectral Proper Orthogonal Decomposition and Gaussian Process Regression
papers.authors: Guglielmo Padula; Antonio Colanera; Gianluigi Rozza
papers.abstract: We present SPOD-GPR, a non-intrusive, parametric, spatio-temporal reduced-order model (ROM) that combines Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), Spectral POD (SPOD), and Gaussian Process Regression (GPR). A parametric POD first projects the high-dimensional state onto a low-dimensional subspace. The reduced trajectories are then divided into windowed sections, transformed into the frequency domain, and truncated to the most energetic frequencies. SPOD is then performed independently at each retained frequency, yielding temporally coherent modes and coefficients. The parametric dependence of the POD and SPOD bases is modelled by GPR on a local chart of the Grassmann manifold after Procrustes alignment. The SPOD modal coefficients are learned both as explicit functions of the parameters and through a parameter-conditioned autoregressive model that allows for temporal extrapolation beyond the training window. Gaussian processes are sampled jointly and pathwise via Matheron conditioning, ensuring that each predictive realization carries uncertainty quantification consistent with the posterior distribution. The method is tested on four parametric examples where the parameter values and the prediction horizon lie outside the training data: the two-dimensional anisotropic Kuramoto--Sivashinsky equation in a time-periodic and a travelling-wave regime, each parametrised by one of its two coefficients; flow past a cylinder parametrised by the Reynolds number; and flow past an elliptic obstacle parametrised by its semi-axes. In all cases, SPOD-GPR reduces the normalised mean absolute error compared to a POD-GPR baseline, and improves the calibration of the predictive uncertainty, especially in the fluid flow cases, where POD-GPR is severely overconfident. This opens the way to spectral, uncertainty-aware reduced-order models for many-query and real-time applications, such as digital twins.

papers.title: Grasp-Taxonomy Conditioning as a Mode Switch for Dexterous Grasping of Climbing Holds
papers.authors: Rumi Loghmani; Abraham George; Amir Barati Farimani
papers.abstract: Dexterous grasping in robotics relies on distinct hand configurations depending on object geometry. We introduce BetaGrasp, a 3D diffusion policy that conditions a DP3-style point-cloud policy on a four-class grasp label (crimp, sloper, pinch, and jug), running on a Franka arm with a 16-DoF LEAP hand. We also introduce a climbing-hold benchmark: a spring testbed whose ratchet gives a slip-force reading in newtons. In our analysis the policy's point-cloud encoder did not separate the four holds, so the scan alone gave it little to choose a grasp from. Without the label (a DP3-style baseline), simulated rollouts from the robot's reset pose all end in a jug grasp, whatever the hold (25% correct grasp type, versus 94% for BetaGrasp). The label works as a switch for which grasp the policy performs. On 80 paired hardware trials, BetaGrasp raises average slip force from 9.6 N to 14.3 N, and grasps slipping fully off the hold drop from 44% of trials to 10%.

papers.title: HIST3R: Decomposing and Rectifying State Updates with History for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
papers.authors: Kenneth Yang; Yu-Chiang Frank Wang
papers.abstract: Streaming 3D reconstruction with recurrent states enables long-video scene understanding under bounded memory, but turns reconstruction into a state-evolution problem: each incoming frame updates a compact scene memory on which all subsequent predictions depend, so unreliable updates overwrite historical context and accumulate into long-horizon geometric drift. We analyze CUT3R-style recurrent updates through a direction--magnitude decomposition, in which the magnitude sets the update gain, i.e., how strongly an observation is written into the state, and the direction encodes the geometric intent, i.e., where the update drives the state. This decomposition provides a unified view of CUT3R and its variants, revealing that existing training-free extensions perform magnitude-only control: they can attenuate an unreliable update but cannot correct its direction. We propose HIST3R, a training-free framework built on CUT3R that controls both components using history. HIST3R rectifies the update direction using locally consistent historical states, and modulates the update magnitude according to the visual discrepancy between the current observation and its history, suppressing redundant updates while preserving complementary evidence. Across camera pose estimation, 3D reconstruction, and video depth estimation, HIST3R consistently improves long-horizon performance while retaining the memory footprint and inference speed of CUT3R. With 1000 input frames, it reduces ATE by 23.87% on ScanNet and 33.65% on TUM-Dynamics relative to the strongest competing method; with 500 frames, it improves median reconstruction accuracy over the strongest CUT3R-based variant by 56.52% on 7-Scenes and 33.96% on NRGBD.

papers.title: Scalable Bayesian Optimization for Efficient Exploration of Moire Patterns
papers.authors: Panagiotis Krokidas; Christos Lazaridis; Vassilis Sioros; Efi-Maria Papia; Vassilios Constantoudis et al.
papers.abstract: Large materials design spaces often contain rare high-performing configurations that are difficult to identify through trial-and-error exploration or purely representative machine-learning (ML) sampling. In this work, we present FruBO, a flexible Bayesian Optimization framework for accelerating the discovery of optimal configurations in computationally demanding materials design problems. As a case study, we investigate multilayer Moiré patterns generated by the superposition of six rotated hexagonal lattices, where the objective is to identify the rotational conformation that maximizes pore-size uniformity, quantified using the Jain fairness index. The resulting benchmark contains 600,000 unique configurations and exhibits a highly skewed objective distribution, making the global optimum difficult to locate by random sampling. We compare random exploration, Gaussian Process-based Bayesian Optimization, and Bayesian Optimization using a lightweight CatBoost surrogate with committee-based uncertainty estimation. Random sampling identifies the global optimum only after 533,012 evaluations, requiring approximately 31 hours, while Gaussian Process-based BO becomes impractical due to GPU memory exhaustion after 290 acquired samples. In contrast, FruBO with CatBoost identifies the global optimum after 1,470 acquired samples and approximately 1.15 hours. These results demonstrate that scalable surrogate models can substantially improve the feasibility and efficiency of BO in large nanomaterials design spaces.

papers.title: SATE: Transferable Spin-Adapted Neural Wavefunctions
papers.authors: Timothy Sereda; Pallas Chou; Morris Hsieh; Emerson Hsieh
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of molecular reactivity requires both accurate and computationally efficient description of electron correlation and spin across various molecular geometries and electronic states. We introduce SATE, a spin-adapted transferable neural wavefunction architecture with effective core potentials. SATE combines a transferable neural wavefunction, the spin-adapted antisymmetrization method, and effective core potentials into a single foundation model architecture pretrained on compositions containing selected elements from hydrogen to bromine. After pretraining and adaptation, our model is able to predict 3d transition-metal spin-state gaps, bond dissociation energies, and reaction energies by addressing two key issues. First, including the core potentials into the model allows us to reduce the number of explicitly treated electrons. Second, using spin-adapted antisymmetrization enforces the prescribed total spin by construction. By testing our model with 3d transition metal chemistry, we evaluate our model's description of strong electron correlation and competing electronic states in such compounds. We find that pretraining improves most tested component energies at matched adaptation budgets, while improvements in spin-state gaps, dissociation energies, and reaction energies remain system dependent. Ultimately, our work lays the foundation for more accurate and transferable modeling of molecular systems by combining the computational efficiency of effective core potentials with explicit control over total spin.

papers.title: A Mathematical Multiscale Framework for Nonlinear Modeling of the Heliosphere
papers.authors: Daniele Telloni; Sabrina Guastavino; Michele Piana
papers.abstract: The inner heliosphere is a highly nonlinear continuous medium where macroscopic ideal magnetohydrodynamics is inextricably coupled with microscopic, fully developed stochastic turbulence. State-of-the-art global 3D numerical solvers, while proficient at capturing the large-scale propagation of extreme space physics phenomena such as coronal mass ejections and corotating interaction regions, are computationally constrained by grid resolution and fundamental partial differential equation formulations. Consequently, they inherently do not resolve the local small-scale turbulent cascade, magnetic intermittency, and localized thermodynamic anomalies. To bridge this fundamental scaleseparation gap, this paper presents a novel mathematical and numerical framework that harmoniously integrates global heliospheric structures with local turbulent physics. The framework generates a highly realistic synthetic continuous medium by superimposing a stochastically driven nonlinear turbulent cascade onto a bimodal deterministic background flow. This cascade reproduces theoretical constraints for fractional power spectral densities, magnetic compressibility, and small-scale intermittency via a discrete multiplicative binomial cascade (p-model). This multiscale continuous background is dynamically perturbed by analytical models of large-scale nonlinear transients, including kinematic shock steepening, continuous current sheet topological reversals, and solar ejecta formalized as asymmetric force-free magnetic flux ropes. By generating exact spatio-temporal arrays across arbitrary distributed coordinates, this unified mathematical model overcomes the spatial degeneracy of single-point observations and provides a computationally efficient analytical baseline for performance models supporting future in-situ multi-spacecraft heliospheric missions, which are currently in their feasibility study phase.

papers.title: CSG-Nav: Confidence-Aware Semantic-Geometric Fusion for Robust Exploration and Accurate Zero-Shot Object-Goal Navigation
papers.authors: Shoubin Chen; Rui Xu; Zehao Wu; Kai Zhang; Tao Huang et al.
papers.abstract: Zero-shot object-goal navigation requires autonomous agents to explore unseen environments and locate target objects without task-specific training, posing challenges in perceptual reliability under observation uncertainty and physically grounded goal termination. Although foundation-model-based approaches improve generalization, they remain vulnerable to unreliable long-range perception, hallucination-induced directional bias, and semantically plausible but geometrically incorrect stopping decisions. To address these limitations, we propose CSG-Nav, a zero-shot navigation framework centered on confidence-aware multimodal information fusion. CSG-Nav integrates three complementary fusion mechanisms. First, semantic-source fusion integrates open-vocabulary detection results, detection confidence, scene observations, and relational reasoning to produce more reliable direction-level semantic scores and suppress hallucination-induced directional bias. Second, spatial-confidence fusion weights multi-view semantic evidence using a Gaussian decay function, suppressing unreliable distant observations while accumulating spatially consistent exploration preferences. Third, semantic-geometric decision fusion combines semantic target detection with depth-based 3D localization to support physically grounded stopping decisions. Experiments on HM3Dv1, HM3Dv2, and MP3D demonstrate competitive zero-shot performance, achieving success rates of 58.9%, 71.6%, and 44.3%. Fusion-level ablations and real-world deployments in indoor and outdoor environments further verify the effectiveness and practicality of CSG-Nav for robust navigation under uncertain perception. Code is available at https://xr-ui.github.io/CSGNav.github.io/

papers.title: Polynomial Sample Complexity of Noninteractive Simulation over Finite Alphabets
papers.authors: Haoran Wang
papers.abstract: We study noninteractive simulation from a finite correlated source. Alice and Bob observe independent copies of the source and generate outputs without communication. We give a quantitative construction for arbitrary finite output alphabets: for every fixed source, a joint law that is simulable with arbitrarily many samples can be approximated using a number of samples polynomial jointly in the output alphabet sizes and the inverse accuracy. We first study binary outputs. A one-sided Wright--Fisher comparison gives a source-dependent explicit exponent and a finite-head Gaussian-threshold representation. We then handle arbitrary finite output alphabets through averaged influence regularity, simplex-preserving Gaussian moment lifting, and a common Gaussian projection for all correlated-prefix states. The sample exponent is independent of the output alphabet sizes. For a concrete biased binary source we certify an explicit exponent below $19$.

papers.title: 3R-Adapter: Retrieval, Rewiring, and Refinement for Efficient Adaptation of 3D Reconstruction Model
papers.authors: Zixiang Ai; Zhenyu Cui; Xu Zou; Jiahuan Zhou
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction models have demonstrated strong generalization under large-scale pre-training, yet they struggle in long-tail scenarios such as low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation. We observe relational attention structure collapse, manifested as the failure of cross-view correspondences, as a primary cause of these limitations. While adaptation offers a practical way to bridge this gap, existing parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) approaches mainly perform channel-wise feature adjustment and lack mechanisms to explicitly adapt relational structures, leaving correspondence failures unresolved. In this work, we formulate adaptation of 3D reconstruction models as a problem of correspondence recovery under domain shift and propose 3R-Adapter, a PEFT paradigm for long-tail 3D reconstruction scenarios. Our method consists of three components: Deformable Retrieval for task-adaptive relation candidate retrieval, Relational Rewiring for reconstructing cross-view relational structures, and Consistency Refinement for injecting the rewired relations into stable predictions. Extensive experiments on low-light reconstruction, joint human-scene reconstruction, and test-time adaptation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves robustness over existing PEFT methods while maintaining efficient lightweight adaptation. Our code is released at https://github.com/PKU-OV3-LAB/3R-Adapter.

papers.title: On the Instance-Specific Sharp Rates for Constrained Least Squares Estimators in the Sequence Model
papers.authors: Zong Shang
papers.abstract: We develop a general methodology based on the Feature Space Decomposition framework for establishing explicit, instance-specific sharp rates for the expected estimation error of convex-constrained least squares estimators in the sequence model, without requiring estimates of localized Gaussian mean widths. We apply this methodology to $\ell_q$ ellipsoids, $\ell_1$ balls, and $kB_1^N\cap B_\infty^N$, obtaining matching upper and lower bounds in the nondegenerate regime. Our methodology also extends beyond Gaussian noise to symmetric noise distributions satisfying a Poincaré inequality. We also provide an elementary proof of the instance-specific sharp rate for isotonic regression for any well-specified signal and any noise level. Combining this result with Han's asymptotic reduction, we further obtain explicit instance-specific sharp convergence rates in probability for isotonic regression in Gaussian linear regression under general signal-dependent asymptotics conditions.

papers.title: Bistatic UAV-Based 3D SAR Imaging Using Integrated Sensing and Communications Transceivers
papers.authors: Akanksha Sneh; Krishna Ayyagari; Vivaswan Nawani; Shobha Sundar Ram
papers.abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) frameworks enable autonomous systems to jointly perform radar sensing and wireless communication using common spectral and hardware resources. Prior art on ISAC-enabled UAV for SAR focused on monostatic configurations for two-dimensional target imaging. In this work, we propose a bistatic UAV tomographic SAR framework in which the IEEE~802.11ad waveform, RF hardware, and spectral resources are jointly utilized for communication and radar sensing for three-dimensional (3D) localization of complex targets. Specifically, we demonstrate how communication packets transmitted from a master ISAC transceiver UAV to a passive receiver UAV are exploited for timing and frequency synchronization, motion compensation, and 3D localization of targets, without requiring auxiliary infrastructure on the passive receiver for these tasks. We evaluate the proposed framework for localizing automotive targets over elevated terrain, with Monte Carlo simulations modeling synchronization and platform motion errors. The results demonstrate improved localization accuracy compared with conventional InSAR-based localization. The interplay between radar and communication performances are further evaluated using diverse modulation schemes.

papers.title: UltraVoxelGS: Voxel-First Feed-Forward Gaussian Splatting for 3D Ultrasound Reconstruction
papers.authors: Yue Wang; Haoxin Chen; Xiaoqing Guo
papers.abstract: We present UltraVoxelGS, a 3D ultrasound reconstruction method that achieves both fast reconstruction and physically faithful rendering for the first time, bringing live spatial feedback during 2D ultrasound scanning within reach. This is made possible by a feed-forward design that predicts a complete Gaussian scene representation from posed ultrasound images directly, entirely bypassing the per-scene optimization bottleneck that has confined prior methods to offline use. Realising such feed-forward prediction in this setting is non-trivial: unlike natural images, ultrasound slices share at most one-dimensional intersections and exhibit view-dependent appearance due to acoustic propagation and attenuation, violating the dense overlap and photometric consistency assumed by existing feed-forward Gaussian methods. Hence, to achieve fast reconstruction, we introduce a feed-forward voxel-to-Gaussian pass that decouples representation size from input count by lifting all posed slices into a fixed-size voxel support and predicting Gaussian parameters directly. For faithful rendering, we propose ultrasound-aware appearance rendering strategy factorize reflection from cumulative attenuation during training and exploit appearance continuity among spatially adjacent slices for efficient Render-time Appearance Adaptation. On both real-world and simulated datasets, UltraVoxelGS achieves best PSNR/SSIM compared with per-scene optimization baselines while reducing inference from 10-20 minutes to approximately 10 seconds (over 35 times faster) and scales to sequences exceeding 1,000 frames. Code is available at https://github.com/YuebyYue/UltraVoxelGS-camera-ready.

papers.title: An Evaluation of Tabular Foundation Models as Training-Free World Models
papers.authors: Xian Yeow Lee; Ryoichi Takase; Ahmed Farahat
papers.abstract: World models are widely considered to be a potential key component of model-based reinforcement learning and robot planning, but typically require task-specific training on substantial interaction data. We investigate whether a pretrained tabular foundation model (TabFM) can serve as a training-free dynamics model for world modeling by framing next-state prediction as in-context regression over transition pairs, and where such a model helps and where it breaks. Across synthetic dynamical systems and robot locomotion benchmarks, TabFM is more accurate than LSTM and MLP models trained from scratch on the same limited transitions in almost all settings, and among regressors fitted to the same data it is the most accurate on locomotion, while a Gaussian process is more accurate on smooth low-dimensional systems. However, models trained on the full dataset remain substantially better on most systems. When rolled out autoregressively over multiple steps, TabFM's accuracy depends strongly on how much context it is given. With a short context, its rollouts quickly degrade to the level of a trivial baseline, whereas with a long context they improve substantially and, on one locomotion task, exceed a trained LSTM. Inference is also about three orders of magnitude slower than an LSTM. Overall, in their current state, we find that training-free priors are useful as predictors when data are scarce and enough context is available, but they are not yet a substitute for trained world models in planning.

papers.title: LO-World: Unified BEV Latent Modeling for Joint 4D Occupancy and LiDAR Forecasting
papers.authors: Zhimin Liao; Ping Wei; Kai Mao; Shuaijia Chen
papers.abstract: LiDAR point clouds and 3D semantic occupancy represent two distinct modalities capturing fine-grained metric geometry and dense volumetric semantics, respectively, holding natural potential for mutual complementarity. However, existing world models typically forecast these modalities independently or cascade them heuristically, missing the opportunity for reciprocal cross-modal regularization. To address this, we propose \textbf{LO-World}, a unified 4D world model that forecasts both modalities within a shared BEV latent space. This single-stream formulation enables dense semantics and metric geometry to mutually reinforce each other, while eliminating multi-pipeline redundancy. Specifically, LO-World couples an efficient hybrid range-voxel autoencoder with a flow-matching generator that caches historical context to reduce iterative sampling latency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LO-World outperforms prior state-of-the-art baselines, improving occupancy forecasting IoU by 10.9% and reducing LiDAR Chamfer Distance by 30.1%. Meanwhile, it sustains a real-time throughput exceeding $25$~FPS on a single RTX 4090. Our code is available at https://github.com/lzzzzzm/LO-World.

papers.title: Capture-Aware Predictive OFDM Reacquisition in Clock-Asynchronous Space-Air-Ground Networks
papers.authors: Zhihan Zeng; Kaihe Wang; Zhongpei Zhang; Chongwen Huang
papers.abstract: Reliable orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) reacquisition must validate an intended burst and return its delay and carrier frequency offset (CFO) correc- tions within capture tolerances. In clock-asynchronous space- air-ground integrated networks (SAGINs), shared geometry and timing uncertainty couples distributed observations, while public- preamble replay creates competing peaks. We propose Capture- Aware Predictive Reacquisition (CAPR), a Bayesian receiver that models competition under both hypotheses and marginalizes unknown spatial interference covariance and target complex amplitude before shared-state fusion. CAPR maximizes posterior probability mass within the capture rectangle and constrains continuous L-BFGS-B refinement through a mass-loss budget. We derive closed-form predictive likelihood reductions, an exact finite-cell action optimizer, a conditional approximation regret bound, and finite-sample false-acceptance calibration. Across 150 primary scenarios and five seeds, CAPR achieves 83.8% strict capture at 4.68% realized false acceptance, improving over Gaussian joint-MAP by 12.5 percentage points overall and 54.2 points across all 32 replay scenarios. Diffuse multipath, degraded assistance, and indistinguishable sources delineate its operational boundaries.

papers.title: Tropical Gaussian Anticoncentration: Optimal Instance-Dependent Bounds for Online Learning in Extensive-Form Games
papers.authors: Ashkan Soleymani; Zhiyuan Fan; Lillian J. Ratliff; Patrick Jaillet; Gabriele Farina
papers.abstract: We study the minimax regret of full-information online decision making in extensive-form games. For prediction with expert advice, the optimal regret is $Θ(\sqrt{T\log K})$, where $K$ is the number of experts, or equivalently, the number of normal-form actions. For treeplex strategy spaces, existing efficient algorithms, including KOMWU and online mirror descent with the weight-one dilated entropy regularizer, achieve regret $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$, where $\mathcal{V}$ is the set of reduced normal-form strategies. We prove that this logarithmic dependence is minimax optimal in the worst-case full-information reward model. The main difficulty is that pure plans in a treeplex are not independent experts: their rewards are correlated through the recursive structure of decisions and observations. To capture this correlation, we introduce tropical Gaussian formulae, recursive Gaussian expressions built from maxima and normalized sums which preserve the variance. The index count of such a formula matches the number of reduced normal-form continuation plans in the corresponding subtree. Our main analytic result shows that every log-balanced tropical Gaussian formula with index count $N$ has Gaussian width $Ω(\sqrt{\log N})$. While a direct approach struggles to recover this lower bound, our proof uses a spherical entropy profile to measure scale-dependent separation among the Gaussian directions, and then applies Turán's theorem and Sudakov minoration to obtain the width lower bound. Applying this result to treeplexes gives an oblivious hard distribution with valid transition outcome and Rademacher terminal rewards, establishing a regret lower bound of $Ω(\sqrt{T\log|\mathcal{V}|})$. This matches known upper bounds up to universal constants and shows that the DilEnt/KOMWU dependence on the reduced normal-form complexity is unavoidable.

papers.title: Accelerating Direct Sparse Solvers with Graph Computing Accelerators
papers.authors: Jiya Su; François-Henry Rouet; Jeff Beisheim; Robert Lucas; Yuqing Wang et al.
papers.abstract: Solving large sparse linear systems by Gaussian elimination is a challenging computational task due to the introduction of non-zero elements, or fill-in. Practitioners use heuristics such as the nested dissection reordering algorithm to try to reduce fill-in. In practice, reordering codes do not achieve the same parallel scaling as factorization, nor can they exploit AVX instructions or GPUs. Thus, reordering can be the primary runtime bottleneck in large-scale computer-aided engineering applications. We consider the use of a novel accelerator, the UpDown system, to accelerate the METIS multilevel nested dissection reordering algorithm. The UpDown system is designed for a broad class of graph computing and irregular algorithms. We report results for small-scale UpDown systems that will be available commercially in 2027, using validated simulation and FPGA emulation platforms. Our findings indicate that small UpDown systems can speed up METIS by two-orders of magnitude versus a single CPU. Compared to ParMETIS on hundreds of MPI ranks, we anticipate the same small UpDown systems offer speedups of 4 - 7, providing the potential to significantly speed finite element simulations

papers.title: An iterated-logarithm price of anytime validity for log-optimal e-processes
papers.authors: Adrien Corenflos
papers.abstract: Log-optimal e-variables at fixed horizons, also called numéraires, have been conjectured to ``almost'' form an e-process for exponential-family null hypotheses. A related open question is whether an e-process can attain the optimal e-power at every horizon up to a bounded loss. Given a final horizon, we study the minimax regret of e-processes relative to the numéraires at all times up to it. For the Gaussian location null and the composite alternative of Gaussian distributions with a smaller variance and an unknown location, we show that the minimax regret in the worst case over the location grows like the iterated logarithm of the final horizon. A single e-process attains this rate at every horizon. This growth answers the question negatively. It also refutes the conjecture if ``almost'' means a regret bounded uniformly over horizons. For this Gaussian location problem, we thus exhibit the frontier precisely: the minimax regret is bounded if and only if the alternatives have at least the variance of the null.

papers.title: Distribution-Free Symmetry Detection in Multi-Reference Alignment at Low SNR
papers.authors: Nir Sharon; Sheng Xu
papers.abstract: Symmetry can reveal the structure of a signal, but detecting it becomes difficult when observations are noisy and randomly transformed. We study how to infer symmetry directly from multi-reference alignment data with additive isotropic Gaussian noise of known variance, without aligning the observations or knowing how the transformations were sampled. For cyclic symmetry, we identify a simple statistical signature that yields tests with exact finite-sample error guarantees. We demonstrate their performance even at very low signal-to-noise ratios. Dihedral symmetry presents a deeper challenge: we show that, for some signals, invariant moments below a sharp order threshold cannot distinguish reflectional from purely rotational symmetry. For generic signals, however, this distinction emerges much earlier. We use these insights to develop tests for dihedral symmetry with asymptotic error control under explicit nondegeneracy conditions. Together, the results clarify what we can learn about symmetry from noisy, unaligned data and suggest a path toward symmetry inference in cryo-EM.

papers.title: Fade to... Red? Scheduling Coloured Noise Exploration Supports Efficient Robot Learning with Reduced Movement Jerk
papers.authors: Francisco M. López; Francisco Cruz
papers.abstract: Exploration in deep reinforcement learning (RL) for continuous control is commonly driven by temporally uncorrelated Gaussian (white) action noise, which leads to jerky motions with locally constrained exploration. In contrast, temporally correlated coloured noise, particularly pink noise, has been shown to support more efficient exploration in RL. Motivated by these findings, we inquire whether scheduling changes to the noise colour over the course of training can outperform white noise for continuous control robotics. We perform a systematic study of 49 linear schedules between white and red noise, together with generalised state-dependent exploration (gSDE), on four sparse-reward manipulation tasks with a Fetch arm and a Shadow Dexterous Hand. We find that the noise colour at the end of training does not affect learning efficiency or end performance, whereas fading towards red noise halves the jerk of exploration in every task. Balancing learning efficiency, end performance and smoothness, red noise emerges as the preferred strategy: it learns as efficiently as pink noise with almost 2-fold less movement jerk. We therefore recommend exploration schedulers that fade towards red noise as the default for off-policy robot learning.

papers.title: DeFSM: Robust and Efficient Decentralization of Federated Submodular Maximization
papers.authors: Duc A. Tran; Dung Truong; Duy Le
papers.abstract: Submodular maximization seeks a small subset best representing a large dataset. In its federated setting, the server is a single point of failure and some clients may be Byzantine. Removing the server raises a trilemma of decentraliza- tion, efficiency, and security. We propose DeFSM, a Byzantine-robust and communication-efficient architecture that replaces the server with a lightweight smart contract and a pool of independent, consensus-free agents. Its aggregation rule, SafeGM, builds on two notions from combinatorial geometry: Tukey depth and safe points (the points lying in the convex hull of the good points wherever the bad points are). SafeGM makes the robust decision on 2D Gaussian random projections, which the contract can compute efficiently, and lifts it back as a convex combination of actual updates. Since lifting loses information, it uses the projected geometric median only when its depth certifies it, and otherwise a Tukey median. The share of bad updates is then bounded only by a count: how many there are, not what they contain. We prove, and confirm empirically, that this bound controls the solution quality. On CIFAR10 and PathMNIST, with up to 30% Byzantine clients and agents, DeFSM never collapses and retains on average about 91% of the quality of the ideal reference, the geometric median at a trusted central server. The geometric median decentralized in its best setting would retain about 96%, but the contract cannot compute it, and so each agent would have to download six times more data, or each client twice as much.

papers.title: The Dusty Circumstellar Structure of the Yellow Hypergiant IRC +10420: Constraints from the SED and Near-Infrared Imaging Polarimetry
papers.authors: Kyung-Won Suh
papers.abstract: The yellow hypergiant IRC +10420 is a post-red supergiant evolving toward higher temperatures. We model its circumstellar dust with the radiative transfer code RADMC-3D, including polarized scattering, constrained by the spectral energy distribution (SED) from 0.4 $μ$m to 1.3 mm and by the K' (2.2 $μ$m) imaging polarimetry of Shenoy et al. (2015), assuming a pole-on view. The model consists of an equatorial structure (a flared inner disk of 0.3 $μ$m grains at 300-3000 au, a ring at 3000-16,000 au whose surface density peaks at $\approx 10^4$ au, and a thin mid-plane disk of 300 $μ$m grains) embedded in a spherical envelope of 0.15 $μ$m grains with $ρ\propto r^{-2.3}$. It reproduces the SED within 0.07 dex and the total- and polarized-intensity profiles; the fractional polarization peaks at 15% at 1.7 arcsec (observed: 14%). The rising surface density of the ring produces the polarized-intensity plateau, and 0.5 $μ$m grains at its outer edge the decline beyond 2 arcsec; grains of $\gtrsim 0.7$ $μ$m are excluded. A thin disk of large grains suggests a settled mid-plane. Stellar temperatures of 7000-8500 K fit equally well. Of the total extinction ($A_V \approx 6.9$ mag), 5 mag is interstellar. Most of the $7.4 \times 10^{-2}$ $M_\odot$ of dust is equatorial; the envelope implies a mass-loss rate of $\approx 10^{-5}$-$10^{-4}$ ($ψ$/100) $M_\odot$ yr$^{-1}$. Because equatorial dust redirects starlight poleward, the pole-on SED overestimates the luminosity by $\approx 1.5$; at the Gaia distance, $L_\star \approx 3.3 \times 10^5$ $L_\odot$. Subtracting a scaled stellar PSF removes most of the nebular light within $\approx 1$ arcsec.

papers.title: Identifiable but Hard to Estimate: Rotation in Equally Spaced Overcomplete ICA
papers.authors: Wenjun Xiao; Yinghao Fang; Hanxin Chen; Sihan Jia; Vince D Calhoun et al.
papers.abstract: How many observations are needed to estimate a common rotation in two-dimensional overcomplete independent component analysis? We study equally spaced mixing columns with known source count, common source law, and column norm. For a fixed non-Gaussian fourth-order Gram-Charlier source law, the rotation is identifiable modulo the column spacing. Yet the sample size for fixed relative angular accuracy grows exponentially with the source count. We characterize this sample size, up to absolute constants, by the reciprocal of the squared Hellinger distance between two rotations separated by half the column spacing. An explicit radially weighted phase estimator attains this scale uniformly over the rotation family, using the observation radius to prevent cancellation in the mean of an angular harmonic. We also determine the exact exponential decay rate of single-observation total variation for the same pair. This gives bounds on the sample size exponent; its exact value remains open. Finally, a noisy binary-source example shows how an exact zero line of the observed characteristic function can have an exponentially small normal derivative.

papers.title: MOTIF: LLM-Defined Material Taxonomies for OOD Property Prediction via Invariant Feature Selection
papers.authors: Gwangseon Jang; Sieun Yun; Dong Ho Lee; Kyong-Ha Lee; Chanuk Lim et al.
papers.abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization remains a central challenge in materials property prediction, where models must extrapolate to novel chemistries beyond the training distribution. While large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong scientific reasoning, their direct use for quantitative prediction remains limited. To address this, we systematically evaluate multiple roles for LLM assistance, finding that only taxonomy-based grouping consistently improves OOD generalization over a strong kNN+GBT baseline. Building on this, we here propose MOTIF, a framework that leverages LLMs not as predictors, but as generators of candidate taxonomies that partition materials into chemically meaningful environments. These taxonomies are evaluated via training-only pseudo-OOD validation, and only those that improve generalization are retained. Invariant feature selection is then applied within each accepted taxonomy, followed by gated aggregation across taxonomies. We evaluate on 2D halide perovskites, where bandgap prediction must generalize across distinct organic spacer families. On this benchmark, MOTIF reduces mean OOD MAE from 0.122 to 0.111 eV. Under a frozen dev/test protocol, the deployable configuration further improves errors from 0.123 to 0.117 eV (electronic bandgap) and from 0.181 to 0.173 eV (optical bandgap). Beyond this primary task, we validate transferability across additional materials datasets, including 3D perovskite solar cell efficiencies and Matbench benchmarks with structure-based splits. Across domains, MOTIF consistently improves robustness under distribution shift, outperforming expert-defined groupings, rule-based heuristics, and clustering baselines, while remaining competitive with strong classical selection methods. These results demonstrate that LLMs are most effective not as predictors, but as tools for discovering structure in data.

papers.title: How Path Integral Diffusion Decides a Finite Spin Glass
papers.authors: Michael Chertkov
papers.abstract: When an AI diffusion-type generator samples a frustrated spin glass, which macroscopic alternatives does it decide first, and when? We study this for bridge-diffusion models of the Path Integral Diffusion (PID) type started from a point source. We show that every isotropic PID is a time-changed Gaussian stochastic localization, and conversely every signal-to-noise schedule is realized by a PID protocol. What a continuous-time generator decides therefore does not depend on the protocol, which only sets when and at what cost. We describe the generator's state by its partial commitments: the probabilities it assigns, at each moment, to nested classes of configurations fixed by the target. The partial commitments are martingales that move only along class contrasts. Their ensemble average gives the information about each level at an exact rate set by squared magnetization contrasts. Each split is decided, approximately, like a binary Gaussian channel at signal-to-noise ratio 1.04/λ_P, with λ_P the leading eigenvalue of the parent's correlation matrix. The theory is applied to Bethe-lattice and Sherrington--Kirkpatrick (SK) glasses with up to 64 spins. It is observed generically that a trajectory first shifts its weight to one of the two mirror halves of the zero-field measure and then to the glassy classes inside it. These classes appear near the glass transition and keep their identity on cooling. Nested glassy levels have similar λ_P and are decided together, so a trajectory commits in one or two distinct events---the mirror choice and a compound glassy decision---which separate further with coupling and size, as the spectra predict. For a generator that takes finitely many steps, the protocol matters through the late, local stage rather than the macroscopic decisions.

papers.title: When Should AI Overturn a Human Decision? Controversy at the 2026 World Cup and a $\sqrt{2/π}$ Solution
papers.authors: Amir Ali Ahmadi; Parsa Alavi; Radeen Alavi
papers.abstract: We study how to combine a human binary call (a referee's offside or onside decision) with an AI numerical measurement (VAR's estimate of an attacker's position relative to the offside line). We derive an explicit maximum-likelihood rule that determines when the referee's call should stand and when a conflicting VAR measurement should overturn it. Our model treats the true offside margin as fixed and unknown and assumes independent additive Gaussian errors in the human's perception and the AI measurement. When both errors have zero means and known standard deviations $σ_H$ and $σ_{AI}$, respectively, the reversal threshold is $\sqrt{2/π}\,σ^2_{AI}/σ_H$. An onside call is overturned precisely when VAR's measured offside margin exceeds this threshold---not merely because VAR places the attacker beyond the offside line. We also derive the rule when either source has a systematic bias. We prove that the maximum-likelihood estimate of the true margin exists and is unique, while the final binary decision requires only a threshold comparison, without computing that estimate numerically. We illustrate the rule through numerical examples and show how to estimate the error parameters from calibration data. The same analysis applies beyond soccer to binary classification problems in which a human call and an AI measurement satisfy the stated model. This paper is intended for educational purposes: we aim to illustrate how undergraduate students and advanced high school students familiar with basic probability and calculus can investigate research questions in AI and its applications.

papers.title: Budget-aware Correspondence-driven View Selection for Real-time 3D Perception of Mobile Robots
papers.authors: Vaishnav Ramesh; Jacob Carter; Shivali J. Patel; Sanjeev J. Koppal; Md Jahidul Islam
papers.abstract: 3D visual perception and scene reconstruction are critical for autonomous robots and intelligent transportation, yet real-world deployments often generate long, redundant image sequences that hinder downstream processing. This report investigates BCVS (budget-aware correspondence-driven view sampling), a pose-free view selection algorithm that offers 22+ FPS on a CPU, enabling online filtering for efficient 3D perception by mobile robots. Unlike existing approaches that rely on full structure-from-motion (SfM) pipelines or camera pose estimation, BCVS employs a purely correspondence-based scoring strategy that prioritizes view novelty while maintaining sufficient overlap for geometric stability. Given a user-specified budget, BCVS iteratively selects the most distinct frames and suppresses near-duplicates, producing compact subsets that preserve connectivity and minimize reconstruction loss. Extensive experiments on benchmark show that BCVS outperforms CPU-friendly baselines at tight budgets and remains competitive as budgets scale. Field trials with large aerial and marine robotics data further validate its practicality and scalability: BCVS reduces redundancy up to 16% while sustaining robust SfM registration and high-quality 3D reconstructions.

papers.title: Wide Field 3D Color Topography for Steep-slope Structures
papers.authors: Yuchen Lin; Mengrui Wang; Fan Li; Jingxiang Zhang; Manming Shu et al.
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) topography measurement is essential for industrial inspection and scientific research. However, existing techniques are limited by an inherent trade-off between resolution, speed, color imaging capability and the ability to measure large-angle surfaces. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel method that integrates ring light illumination based wide-field 3D imaging with an iterative shape-from-focus (SFF) algorithm. The system employs coaxial epi-illumination combined with ring light illumination to simultaneously acquire information from flat regions and steep slopes. The proposed iterative SFF algorithm achieves high-resolution 3D topography measurement. Full-color 3D reconstructions of electronic chips and PCBs demonstrate that the proposed method enables fast scanning and sub-micrometer resolution and significantly extending the measurable inclination range for large-angle structures. This method fills a critical gap in existing technology for fast, natural-color, 3D imaging and measurement of samples with steep topographies.

papers.title: On the sharp weak-type inequality for Riesz transforms
papers.authors: Rodrigo Bañuelos; Mähdi Hormozi; Alexander Volberg
papers.abstract: We prove that the weak-type $(1,1)$ norm of each classical Riesz transform $R_j$, $j=1,\dots,n$, on real-valued inputs on $\R^n$ and $\T^n$ is $\KD$. The constant $\KD=π^2/(8\Gcat)$, where $\Gcat$ is Catalan's constant, was obtained by Davis \cite{Davis1974} for the Hilbert transform on $\R$ and the conjugate-function operator on the circle $\T$. The Burkholder--Bellman function argument also applies to coordinate Riesz transforms of product generators. If $-L$ generates a symmetric sub-Markov semigroup on a nonzero standard $σ$-finite measure space $Y$, then $-\partial_x(-\partial_x^2+L)^{-1/2}$ has the same exact norm on both $\mathbb R\times Y$ and $\mathbb T\times Y$. The derivative acts in the ordinary line or circle factor, while $L$ governs the independent transverse variables. An explicit integral inequality strengthens the weak-type estimate and bounds the truncated second moment of the transform. The general theorem applies to Gaussian, Dunkl, Laguerre, Jacobi, Schrödinger, and Laplace--Beltrami transverse generators, finite reversible chains, and subordinated semigroups.

papers.title: Three-dimensional polarization of thermal fields at arbitrary distances from thin-film emitters
papers.authors: Xiaohong Zhang; Wenshan Cai; Zhuomin Zhang
papers.abstract: Recent advances have shown that thermal radiation can exhibit strong polarization in both the near and far fields. However, most existing studies focus on paraxial far-field emission, where polarization can be described using conventional two-dimensional (2D) Stokes parameters. Non-paraxial thermal radiation, with three nonzero vector components, requires a fully three-dimensional (3D) polarization description. This work develops a generalized theoretical method for analyzing thermal-radiation polarization at arbitrary distances from an emitter. Fluctuation-dissipation theory is employed to determine the $3\times3$ coherence matrix of the thermally emitted electromagnetic field, from which generalized 3D Stokes parameters are obtained. This method is applied to planar slabs composed of isotropic, anisotropic, and nonreciprocal materials. The results reveal distinct polarization behavior across the near- and far-field regimes. Near-field polarization is strongly influenced by evanescent waves and polariton dispersion, whereas far-field polarization is primarily governed by polarization-dependent radiative properties, including differences between transverse-electric (TE) and transverse-magnetic (TM) emission. Slab thickness further modifies polarization by controlling supported modes and interference effects. In addition, circular polarization, which vanishes in reciprocal slabs, is observed in n-type doped InAs under an external magnetic field that breaks reciprocity. This work provides a unified framework for characterizing the polarization of thermal electromagnetic fields from the extreme near field to the far field.

papers.title: McKean--Vlasov Diffusions from Liouville Spectral Green Response
papers.authors: Chunhao Cai
papers.abstract: For Dirichlet Liouville Brownian motion with $0<γ<2$, the Gaussian response of a finite vector of logarithmic eigenvalues determines a conditional Green energy. We weight this energy by the current spectral density in the fixed reference space. The resulting self-consistent evolution is a porous-medium equation for the canonical spectral form. We construct its positive probability flow, prove an energy identity, and pass from the regularized response forms to the Green limit. The energy identity yields strong convergence of the Gaussian gradients and of the conditional response drifts. A superposition argument then realizes the flow as a McKean--Vlasov weak diffusion.

papers.title: Isoperimetric comparison for surfaces with nonnegative curvature and uniformly convex boundary
papers.authors: Chao Xia; Jincong Zheng
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp relative isoperimetric comparison for compact surfaces with nonnegative Gaussian curvature and smooth nonempty boundary whose geodesic curvature is at least 1. We prove that the normalized relative isoperimetric profile for such a surface is bounded below by that of the Euclidean unit disk, with equality holding at some area fraction in (0,1) if and only if the surface is isometric to the unit disk. The proof uses a differential comparison argument for the isoperimetric profile, based on a suitable non-constant normal variation of isoperimetric curves inspired by the model geometry.

papers.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. II. A convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations for real-space pair-density representability
papers.authors: Maho Nakata
papers.abstract: Variational second-order reduced-density-matrix calculations can dissociate molecules into fractionally charged fragments; Part I largely removed this failure with integer electron-count conditions on fixed partitions. Building on the realizability theory of point processes, we place these conditions in a convergent hierarchy of rigorous relaxations, defined by finite occupation linear programs (LPs) on spatial partitions, for real-space pair densities at fixed one-particle density. Every level contains all representable pair densities, the levels tighten under nested refinement, and their intersection characterizes pair densities admitting a symmetric $N$-particle probability-measure extension. In a fixed orbital basis the levels give monotonically increasing lower bounds to the full configuration-interaction energy, which they need not reach, even for the Coulomb repulsion. The spin-summed real-space cuts of Part I are its two-cell members. The LP optimum is also a measure: at fixed one-particle density it equals the $L^1$ distance of the coarse-grained candidate from representability and increases under refinement to that of the candidate, with a vanishing coarse-graining error; its primal law constructs a representable approximation, and its dual a violated valid inequality, used as a cut in molecular calculations. The count conditions are not implied by the usual positivity conditions: moment data that satisfy all three-particle positivity conditions, including $T_1$ and $T_2$, give through Gaussian orbitals a smooth pair density that violates an integer count. For atoms at fractional electron number, ensemble relaxations with the integer-count condition lie closer to the exact piecewise-linear energy than the zero-variance fixed-$N$ form.

papers.title: SurgTAP-3D: A Large-Scale Cross-Surgery Video Dataset with Contact-Aware 3D Motion Tracking
papers.authors: Jiaxin Guo; Wenzhen Dong; Taoyu Wu; Haomin Kuang; Mengya Xu et al.
papers.abstract: Understanding 3D scene dynamics in minimally invasive surgery (MIS) is a fundamental step toward physically intelligent and autonomous surgical systems. However, existing public datasets offer limited scalability and diversity in real-world clinical scenarios. Moreover, annotations typically focus on either tissue or instruments alone, overlooking tool-tissue interactions. This gap limits applications such as augmented reality guidance and autonomous surgery driven by vision-language-action (VLA) models or world models, which demand large-scale, high-quality 3D supervision. In this work, we construct SurgTAP-3D, a large-scale in-vivo pseudo-3D surgical motion tracking dataset and benchmark, comprising 520K frames, 4,549 action clips, and 1.4M 2D/3D point trajectories from diverse robotic and manual procedures under unified action categories. To make annotation scalable, we design a unified framework for surgical 3D point tracking that converts uncalibrated monocular surgical videos into structured 4D annotations through contact-region prompting, active-tool segmentation, dynamic bundle adjustment, and global 4D refinement. This pipeline adapts foundation priors to surgical videos and produces temporally consistent trajectories, pseudo-scale geometry, camera poses, and instrument masks. The dataset captures realistic challenges inherent to surgical environments, including occlusions, smoke, bleeding, and rapid instrument motion.
