For Gaussian sketches, we obtain an explicit high-probability population-risk bound, showing that row subsampling is not the only possible communication-statistics tradeoff for networked information aggregation.

papers.title: Efficient 3D plant segmentation through multiscale graph learning and optimized geometric processing
papers.authors: Jesus Ivan Ruiz-Martinez; Andres Mendez-Vazquez; Eduardo Rodriguez-Tello
papers.abstract: Plant organ segmentation on compact computing platforms requires accurate predictions and affordable geometric preparation. We develop and evaluate a multiscale edge based graph attention model that combines local shape descriptors, two neighborhood scales and a residual stem and leaf correction in approximately 78 thousand parameters. The engineering application is plant point cloud segmentation for precision agriculture, assessed through grouped accuracy experiments and physical Raspberry Pi 5 inference. Broad comparisons with hierarchical, graph and transformer baselines establish PointNeXt as the strongest external accuracy reference among the tested local recipes. A nested four variant ablation on a local maize collection separates geometric information from the combined multiscale configuration across seven outer groups and three seeds. The complete model achieves the highest mean intersection over union, 86.36%, although uncertainty and boundary errors qualify the contribution of each component. We then optimize full cloud principal component analysis, sampling and neighbor queries without changing learned weights or descriptor definitions. All 1,180 paired desktop comparisons on PlantNet and TomatoWUR preserve exact logits and predictions. Multiscale pipeline latency falls from 330.33 to 96.82 milliseconds on PlantNet and from 1,054.52 to 463.10 milliseconds on TomatoWUR. PointNeXt also benefits from optimized sampling and remains faster over the complete pipeline. These results support compact graph learning with reduced geometric overhead, while physical board measurements establish inference feasibility rather than energy efficiency or readiness for autonomous flight.

papers.title: Bayesian transfer for offline Q-learning with multi-task Gaussian processes
papers.authors: Wenxing Guo
papers.abstract: Offline reinforcement learning can benefit from data collected in related tasks, yet indiscriminate knowledge transfer may lead to negative transfer under task mismatch and limited target-data coverage. We propose a target-aware Bayesian transfer framework for offline Q-learning based on multi-task Gaussian processes that jointly model task-specific Q-functions. Source tasks are assessed using target predictive evidence and maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), while posterior uncertainty and behavior-supported action sets guide conservative Bellman updates and policy extraction. To account for the dependence induced by Bellman bootstrapping, we distinguish Bellman innovations from bootstrap errors and establish stability and predictive source-selection results under explicit regularity conditions. We further derive selection-adaptive posterior contraction and offline policy-performance bounds, identifying the structural conditions under which source information can be pooled to achieve minimax-optimal rates in a shared-function Gaussian sequence experiment. Simulation studies with heterogeneous source tasks demonstrate improved target Q-function estimation and reduced material negative transfer compared with indiscriminate source pooling. An application to human decision-making data further shows higher average expected immediate payoff than both target-only learning and matched-size random source selection. These results highlight the benefits of combining target-aware source selection with uncertainty-aware conservative learning for reliable and sample-efficient offline reinforcement learning.

papers.title: Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Pre-training
papers.authors: Szymon Płotka; Gizem Mert; Pedro R. A. S. Bassi; Wenxuan Li; Zongwei Zhou et al.
papers.abstract: Medical Vision-Language Pre-training (VLP) leverages the semantic richness of radiology reports to learn 3D representations, yet current architectures remain fundamentally anatomy-agnostic. While clinical diagnostics rely on organ-specific context, standard encoders apply a uniform, dense parameterization to all volumetric patches, and existing Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) routers gate on isolated local features without explicit access to the organ composition of the scan or crop. We propose Anatomy-Activated Mixture-of-Experts (A$^{2}$MoE), a framework that incorporates anatomical inductive biases within the model's computational path. A$^{2}$MoE introduces two key components: (1) a Histogram Representation Router (HRR) that conditions expert selection on global visual context and a predicted anatomical composition histogram, encouraging anatomy-dependent expert weighting; and (2) an Organ-Query Multi-Scale Projector (OQMSP) that utilizes learnable queries to extract organ-level embeddings for fine-grained alignment without requiring manual annotations at inference. By routing at the patch level rather than the token level, A$^{2}$MoE reduces routing complexity by orders of magnitude while satisfying load balancing by construction. Pre-trained on over 60,000 multi-phase CT scans, A$^{2}$MoE achieves state-of-the-art performance across segmentation, classification, and detection benchmarks. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our anatomically grounded inductive biases support robust generalization to MRI and ultrasound, establishing a scalable foundation for medical representation learning. The code is available at https://github.com/gmum/A2MoE.

papers.title: In-Band Boundary Resonances from Coalescing Zero-Group-Velocity Points
papers.authors: Amir Rajabpoor Alisepahi; Charles A. Downing; Jihong Ma
papers.abstract: Boundary states generally reside in band gaps, whereas in-band confinement typically requires exact decoupling from propagating modes. We demonstrate an alternative mechanism in reciprocal, topologically trivial Hermitian lattices arising from the coalescence of two zero-group-velocity (ZGV) points. At coalescence, the group velocity and inverse effective mass vanish simultaneously, and the corresponding Bloch root acquires higher multiplicity. The coalesced root remains propagating, whereas nearby root splitting yields weakly evanescent channels that, together with a bulk-matched termination, generate a boundary-weighted resonance within the propagating spectrum. The mechanism is realized analytically in a two-leg ladder model through the coalescence of time-reversal-related ZGVs and extends to distinct ZGVs produced by longer-range interactions. Finite-size scaling distinguishes the resulting resonance from extended and defect-bound states. Scanning laser Doppler vibrometry on a 3D-printed elastic ladder reveals boundary enhancement in a nearly flat band region, consistent with operation slightly below criticality. ZGV coalescence thus provides a bulk framework for in-band boundary resonances in reciprocal Hermitian lattices.

papers.title: Beyond Host-Side Control: HBM Controller Partitioning Across Host and HBM Base Dies
papers.authors: Tharunya Yogananda; Wantong Li
papers.abstract: Recent generations of high bandwidth memory (HBM), such as HBM4, allow the base die of the memory stack to be manufactured using a logic process that can accommodate more complex controller functions next to the DRAM. We present the first systematic quantitative study of function-level controller placement between the host and the HBM4 base die on a silicon interposer. We divide the controller into its main functions and evaluate four placements, from a complete host controller to a complete base die controller, with intermediate placements that move maintenance or scheduling to the base die. We extend Ramulator 2 with HBM4 timing and maintenance, model a die-to-die (D2D) link with timing checks at the DRAM interface, and compose area, energy, and temperature from synthesized controller blocks, modeled storage, and interface data. A provisioned D2D link preserves per-stack bandwidth and adds about twice its one-way delay to unloaded latency. Maintenance moves to the base die with no bandwidth cost and frees host command slots, and the freed share grows with stack height. Replacing the wide interface with a D2D link saves 61% of host shoreline and 16.85 mm2 of host area per stack. The D2D link dominates the added base die area and power, and the base die runs cooler under streaming with link energy below 0.4 pJ/bit. Shared control delivers up to 1.72x the throughput of static partitioning between two requestors.

papers.title: Polynomial-Preserving Processes and Volatility Modelling in Discrete Time
papers.authors: Maciej Augustyniak; Alexandru Badescu; Zekun Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper develops a discrete-time framework for volatility modelling and derivative pricing based on polynomial preservation. The framework provides exact moments of arbitrary order and serial cross-moments of variance and return processes over any finite horizon through finite-dimensional matrix representations. This analytical tractability is maintained while accommodating flexible leverage and variance-of-variance dynamics and non-Gaussian innovations. We introduce two novel classes of stochastic volatility models that nest widely used discrete-time specifications and study their statistical properties. Under two distinct scaling regimes, we establish weak convergence to polynomial diffusions and jump-diffusions and convergence of polynomial moments, linking discrete-time moment recursions to continuous-time matrix-exponential formulas. An empirical analysis of S\&P~500 returns and a large panel of options spanning 1996--2023 shows that the proposed specifications improve return fit and reduce mean weekly implied volatility root mean squared errors by approximately 8--41\% relative to their nested benchmarks, depending on the variance dynamics and innovation distribution.

papers.title: Three-dimensional multipole states of the Bose-Einstein condensate of polar molecules in a shallow two-dimensional trapping potential
papers.authors: S. Sanjay; S. Saravana Veni; Boris A. Malomed
papers.abstract: We investigate the formation, stability, and dynamics of three-dimensional (3D) elongated multipole quantum droplets (QDs) in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) of polar molecules with long-range interactions between molecular electric dipoles. The condensate is confined by a 2D trapping potential, which is a combination of the harmonic-oscillator potential and a central Gaussian potential hill. The system is modeled by an extended Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation, incorporating the dipole-dipole interactions and beyond-mean-field Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) correction, which play a crucial role in stabilizing self-bound QD structures. In regimes of weak and strong confinement, stable multipole states with the number of lobes $n=2S$ are created by means of the imaginary-time-propagation (ITP) method from inputs with vorticity $S\leq 2$. The so created multipole QDs carry no angular momentum. Stable higher-order multipole states can be produced by the ITP method from inputs with $S\geq 3$ up to $S=6$ (i.e., $2S=12$ lobes) only under strong confinement and when the molecule number $N$ exceeds a threshold value. We analyze the dependence of the chemical potential, energy per particle, and peak density on $N$ and $S$ in the weak- and strong-confinement regimes. A noteworthy fact is that, below another threshold value of $N$, the minimum-energy (ground) state is created by the input with $S=1$, rather than $S=0$. Simulations of perturbed evolution reveal that, despite satisfying energetic stability criteria, only a subset of the multipole QDs are truly stable, with higher-order ones tending to develop instabilities or relax toward lower-order states. These results highlight the essential roles of the trapping potential, anisotropy of the dipole-dipole interactions, and LHY-induced repulsion in the formation and structural stability of multipole QDs.

papers.title: Bayesian Wombling for Tracking Invasive Species
papers.authors: Aritra Halder; Joseph R. Stinziano; Joshua Persi
papers.abstract: This paper develops Bayesian wombling, or boundary analysis for tracking invasive species. We focus on three invasive species of concern in North America: Lycorma delicatula, Adelges tsugae, and Microstegium vimineum. We aim to demonstrate the applicability of wombling for supporting invasive pest management activities. In spatial science wombling is used widely to track regions of rapid change within the spatial reference domain. We use Gaussian process models for point-referenced spatial data followed by predictive inference on rates of change over curves using line integrals. We extend the wombling model based Bayesian inference framework to feature simple analytic forms that avoid high dimensional quadrature while offering uncertainty quantification over curvilinear spatial boundaries.

papers.title: Stochastic Port-Hamiltonian Gaussian Processes for Learning from Noisy Dynamics on Lie Groups
papers.authors: Thribhuvan Rapolu; Luke McLennan; Chandrajit Bajaj
papers.abstract: Learning predictive models for dynamics is difficult because observations are often sparse and noisy, while the underlying dynamics evolve on nonlinear configuration manifolds and are affected by environmental dissipation and stochastic disturbances. Standard neural dynamics models can fit short-term trajectories but often violate physical structure, accumulate error over long horizons, or rely on parameterizations that introduce singularities such as gimbal lock. We introduce LieSPHGP, a stochastic Gaussian-process framework for learning rigid body dynamics with port-Hamiltonian structure and stability-aware robustness. LieSPHGP represents motion on Lie groups and Lie algebras, enabling coordinate-consistent optimization without singular parameterizations. Learned mass, potential energy, dissipation, and control components retain physical roles and a separate diffusion term represents stochastic forcing. Each component is modeled by Matérn kernel Gaussian processes which capture uncertainty induced by noisy observations. To improve physical validity, Lie group exponential map updates preserve rotational constraints, while positive-definite damping ensures nonnegative deterministic energy dissipation. The implicit-explicit integrator additionally provides unconditional stability for the frozen linear damping subsystem. The resulting model learns predictive dynamics that are robust to noise, respect rigid body geometry, and capture both intrinsic motion and environmental dissipation. Experiments on various noisy rigid body benchmarks show improved prediction accuracy, stronger long-horizon stability, and better satisfaction of manifold constraints compared with neural dynamics baselines. Code, data and interactive results are available on the project website: https://thribhuvanrapolu.github.io/liesphgp/

papers.title: Structurally Separated DAG Learning with Multi-Scale Normalized Closure
papers.authors: Shuai Feng; Hao Yan
papers.abstract: Continuous DAG learning commonly enforces acyclicity through scalar functions of a weighted adjacency that aggregate evidence from weighted closed walks. We add a complementary layer: matrix-valued closure logits---explicit multi-hop structural relation scores for each ordered pair---supervised alongside data fit, sparsity, and a DAGMA-style barrier on the weighted adjacency. The distinction is not scalarization of the overall objective but how path evidence is represented and exposed before aggregation. SMNC (scale-normalized multi-scale closure) builds these scores on a structural gate by repeated squaring in log space and divides each scale by its path-length budget, counteracting product-style attenuation along long cycles; diagonal entries support node-wise cycle supervision and off-diagonals optional pairwise reachability cues. In the linear model, a bounded structure--magnitude factorization ties strong effective edges to strong gates; a nonlinear induced gate offers another construction with the same intent. For sufficiently strong cycles, normalized logits admit a length-independent lower bound; under a unique-active-cycle assumption, the hard final-scale readout yields a polynomial log-gate gradient factor rather than exponential product-style decay. On cue-free, unstandardized Gaussian linear and nonlinear ER benchmarks, these models improve over DAGMA, run with default hyperparameters at a reduced budget, on denser graphs and are close to it on sparse ones.

papers.title: Polynomial Denoisers on the Image Manifold: Volterra Networks for Self-Contained Pixel Diffusion
papers.authors: Siddharth Roheda; Rohit Chowdhury; Amit Satish Unde; Aniruddha Bala
papers.abstract: Natural images are often conjectured to lie on a low-dimensional manifold within the high-dimensional pixel space. Recent work leverages this to build self-contained pixel-space diffusion models without specialized machinery or pretrained components. A plain Transformer on raw image patches suffices, provided it predicts the clean image rather than the noise and compresses each patch through an aggressive bottleneck. The mixing operator, however, has remained softmax attention, inherited from sequence modeling rather than derived from denoising. For Gaussian noise, the optimal denoiser admits a canonical expansion in polynomial functionals of the observation, the Wiener--Volterra series. We prove that softmax attention, and any normalized mixing rule (including linear attention), cannot realize any polynomial map beyond an affine one. In contrast, Volterra layers realize this class directly and, on a data manifold, achieve approximation rates governed by the manifold dimension rather than the ambient pixel dimension. We therefore propose the architecture these results prescribe; raw image patches passed through a bottleneck embedding, followed by cascaded low-rank Volterra layers, which carry no activation function because each layer is nonlinear in its own right. To our knowledge this is the first pixel-space diffusion architecture whose mixing operators are Volterra layers throughout, with no attention, no convolution, no pretrained components, and no activation function on the residual path. On ImageNet $256 \times 256$ and $512 \times 512$, the resulting model is competitive with self-contained pixel-space diffusion at matched parameter and FLOP budgets.

papers.title: Efficient SC-Flip Decoding for Polar Codes through Decision-Boundary Normalization
papers.authors: Gulinisha Yiming; Zhongjun Yang; Zhicheng Liu; Zhiming Ma; Xumin Ni et al.
papers.abstract: Accurate first erroneous position (FEP) identification is key to improving the error-correction performance of successive cancellation flip (SCF) decoding. However, FEP identification remains challenging with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. To address this issue, we propose decision-boundary normalization (DBN) to improve FEP identification and develop a novel DBN-SCF decoding algorithm. DBN normalizes the magnitude of each decision log-likelihood ratio (LLR) by the standard deviation predicted by the Gaussian approximation (GA) for the corresponding bit-channel. This allows a single normalized threshold to be shared across bit-channels within each code configuration, giving it a consistent statistical meaning and avoiding per-channel calibration. DBN-SCF decoding selects candidate flip positions from the information set in the natural successive cancellation (SC) decoding order using a threshold, without sorting. Moreover, DBN-SCF decoding achieves better error-correction performance with a limited number of re-decoding attempts. It also requires lower average decoding complexity than existing SCF decoding methods at a comparable level of error-correction performance.

papers.title: AmodalBox: Automated 3D Bounding Box Annotation under Partial Visibility
papers.authors: In-Jae Lee; Namtae Kim; Robert Exley; Kwonyoung Ryu; Jaesik Park
papers.abstract: Recent progress in vision foundation models (VFMs) has made automated open-vocabulary 3D bounding box annotation increasingly feasible by jointly leveraging LiDAR point clouds and images. However, partial observations remain a major challenge in sparse driving scenes, where visible LiDAR points often cover only a small fraction of the object's surface and provide insufficient cues for estimating its full spatial extent. As a result, existing methods often produce mislocalized boxes or leave objects unlabeled. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{\Ours{}}, an automated annotation framework that leverages image-generated 3D assets as amodal geometric priors for partially observed objects. By establishing correspondences between input images and rendered views of 3D assets, \Ours{} robustly aligns canonical amodal geometry with partially observed world-space LiDAR point clouds. To improve temporal consistency and reduce computational cost, \Ours{} generates a single asset per instance, estimates its metric scale once at a single frame and propagates it across frames for dynamic instances, and aggregates multi-frame observations for static instances. 3D object detectors trained on annotations from \Ours{} improve performance over strong baselines by 14.1 mAP on the nuScenes dataset and by 12.45 AP at IoU 0.5 for the vehicle class on the Waymo Open Dataset (WOD). Our project page is available at: \href{https://oliver0922.github.io/AmodalBox/}{https://oliver0922.github.io/AmodalBox/}

papers.title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory
papers.authors: Manisha Rajput; Farhan Ahmed Siddique; Chung-Che Huang; Ioannis Zeimpekis; Sayani Majumdar
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. A FeFET with two-dimensional (2D) channel provides the opportunity for better electrostatic gate control and scalability beyond silicon. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. FeFETs based on 2-3 monolayer Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) channel and a 20 nm HZO back gate oxide layer exhibit a large hysteresis with a memory window spanning 4.4 V under a operating voltage range of +3.8 to -3.8 V, and an ION/IOFF ratio of 10^5. We demonstrate that the polarization charge-induced modification of Schottky barrier width strongly affects the hole transport and memory properties of MoS2-HZO FeFETs. We further demonstrate several advantages and unique features of the FeFETs such as nondestructive data readout, non-volatile data retention under zero gate bias, low operation voltage, high write endurance and ultra-fast switching speed. These 1T memory cells can simplify the dense 3D integrated array architecture and offer additional practical functionalities, such as fast programming and erasing of large data arrays that are absent for many conventional memories. The demonstrated MoS2 and HZO-based FeFET shows great potential for on-chip complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible circuits for multifunctional devices, especially for 3D monolithically integrated architectures for AI workload.

papers.title: BP-based qLDPC Decoding under Long-range Correlated Noise: Trapping Configurations and Prior Mismatch
papers.authors: Abhinav Dangi; Avhishek Chatterjee
papers.abstract: We study the robustness of two state-of-the-art BP-based qLDPC decoders, Relay-BP and beam search, designed for independent noise when applied to spatially correlated noise with unchanged single-mechanism error probabilities. We generate correlated errors with a hidden Gaussian Markov random field, which lets us control the strength and range of the correlation while keeping every marginal error probability exact. This setting complements correlation-aware decoding: it asks how existing decoders perform when their assumed joint error model is mismatched. Across multiple tested circuits and code instances that we simulated, we observe that correlations can change logical error rates by orders of magnitude, reduce the finite-size distance advantage, and alter the relative ranking of Relay-BP, beam search, and BP-OSD. On one of the two tested circuits, Relay-BP and beam search become worse than BP-OSD, and increasing relay memory or beam width does not compensate for the degradation. Configuration analysis indicates that correlation primarily increases the probability of trapping configurations that are known to challenge these decoders; at matched error weight, correlated errors still cause decoding failures several times more often than i.i.d. errors. Finally, supplying the decoders with the marginals conditioned on the hidden field recovers most of the lost performance in the tested settings identifying prior mismatch as a major contributor to performance degradation under correlation.

papers.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
papers.authors: Juanxi Tian; Jiadong Hou; Baiang Li; Xin Lin; Zhengbo Jiao et al.
papers.abstract: Visual generative models increasingly blur the line between synthesizing observations and simulating environments. Yet visual plausibility alone does not constitute successful world modeling: compelling outputs may lack persistent state, physical dynamics, or causally consistent responses to interactions. We define a generative world model as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories that reflect outcomes under observed and counterfactual interventions. From this definition, we derive an intelligence-oriented framework spanning perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction. We present WorldFoundry, open-source infrastructure for reproducible inference and evaluation across video, 3D and 4D, embodied action, and interactive world systems. WorldFoundry unifies model and benchmark discovery, runtime and asset preparation, execution orchestration, artifact management, and interactive visualization, while modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. Explicit manifests, durable artifact contracts, and evidence-aware scorecards separate execution readiness from evaluative claims, making each claim traceable to its supporting artifacts. The catalog contains 270 model entries, 74 benchmarks, and 62 registered metric entries, with readiness and execution evidence recorded separately. WorldFoundry enables reproducible comparison of persistent, controllable dynamics across heterogeneous systems, advancing the field from perceptual synthesis toward measurable world intelligence.

papers.title: BlenderFORGE: Framework for Optimizing Reactive 3D-Graphics Editing Ability of MLLMs
papers.authors: Zilin Guo; Tianrui Zhang; Yi Rong; Yichen Liu; Yuxin Guo et al.
papers.abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown promise as interactive agents, yet precise, programmatic 3D graphics editing remains difficult to train because existing systems largely rely on closed-source model APIs and lack deterministic, state-verifiable execution environments. We present BlenderFORGE, a trainable data-environment-optimization framework for open-weight MLLM agents that edit explicit Blender scenes through Blender Python (bpy) code generation. BlenderFORGE targets four fundamental state-verifiable editing task families: object placement, shape-key editing, lighting adjustment, and material modification. It integrates three components: (1) a scalable perturbation-based data generation pipeline built from curated assets and large-scale 3D scene repositories; (2) an isolated Blender Sandbox for deterministic code execution, structured state export, and closed-loop reward computation; and (3) a two-stage training pipeline that uses offline teacher trajectories for cold-start Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and sandbox-computed rewards for multi-turn tool-agentic Reinforcement Learning (AgentLoop-RL). Experiments across the four task families show that the resulting open-weight Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5-9B BlenderFORGE agents substantially improve over their base models and achieve competitive performance with several zero-shot proprietary MLLM baselines on selected metrics. Additional cross-benchmark evaluations and camera-reframing experiments provide evidence of transfer beyond the original training setting.

papers.title: Simultaneous 3D acoustic modulation and imaging of proton-induced nanodroplet vaporization for proton therapy monitoring
papers.authors: Sophie V. Heymans; Bram Carlier; Marcus Ingram; Kenneth Poels; Marc Desmaret et al.
papers.abstract: Superheated nanodroplets exposed to ionizing radiation vaporize into echogenic microbubbles, enabling ultrasound-based radiation therapy monitoring and proton range verification. However, at body temperature, decafluorobutane nanodroplets are insensitive to primary protons, and vaporize only when traversed by rare heavy secondary particles, limiting the in vivo applicability of this concept. We previously demonstrated that acoustic modulation at pressures well below the Acoustic Droplet Vaporization threshold can transiently increase nanodroplet sensitivity to radiation, enabling vaporization by primary protons. However, as acoustic modulation was applied by a focused single-element transducer, sensitization was restricted to a small region of the irradiated volume, and monitoring required an additional imaging probe. Here, we introduce a compact implementation that combines wide-field acoustic modulation and volumetric imaging on the same large-element matrix array, enabling simultaneous nanodroplet sensitization to protons and vaporization monitoring across the entire irradiated volume. The resulting 3D vaporization maps were fitted to the proton stopping distribution to estimate beam position and width parameters. At body temperature and starting from acoustic pressures as low as 122 kPa, we observed a transition from a response dominated by secondary particles to a response dominated by primary protons. The resulting vaporization peak at the proton range enabled sub-millimeter range estimation and detection of a 1.05 mm range shift with both accuracy and precision below 0.2 mm. These results demonstrate proton range verification and 3D treatment monitoring with acoustically-modulated decafluorobutane nanodroplets and represent an important step towards the envisioned clinical application.

papers.title: Quadratic Bezier Splatting with Structural Initialization for Efficient Painting Rendering
papers.authors: Jinfan Liu; Xuhan Zhan; Mengqin Zhao; Guangyi Deng; Wuze Zhang et al.
papers.abstract: Stroke-based rendering is often optimized as a pixel-level reconstruction task. This over-reliance on global error reduction not only degrades strokes into fragmented curves due to a lack of structured planning, but also allows locally defective primitives to be concealed by overlapping layers. To address these issues, we introduce a model-guided framework for stroke-audited rendering. Our framework uses Quadratic Bezier Splatting to analytically model continuous curved strokes with efficient differentiable alpha compositing. Built on this renderer, a feedforward multi-scale stroke decoder provides a structural initialization with learned stroke-scale allocation, while test-time stroke optimization supplies the reconstruction capacity needed for high-fidelity refinement. We further propose a single-stroke audit mechanism that explicitly evaluates local stroke quality, preventing defective primitives from surviving optimization through layer-wise compensation. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves coherent layouts, improves PSNR by up to 5.46 dB, yields a 16% more compact representation, and accelerates combined renderer forward and backward computation by a factor of 220.3.

papers.title: Probing Chern Topology through Hall-Sensitive Photonic Spin Hall Shifts in a d-wave Altermagnet
papers.authors: Mahnoor Sajid; Maha Siddiqui; Muzamil Shah
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the photonic spin Hall effect in a two-dimensional Rashba-coupled $d$-wave altermagnetic Chern system subjected to a uniform out-of-plane exchange field. We first analyze the energy-band structure and the Dirac mass distribution at the high-symmetry points, where $m_Γ=m_M=Δ_x, m_X=Δ_x-4 t_J$, and $m_Y=Δ_x+4 t_J$. Band inversions at high-symmetry points generate both a topologically trivial regime $(C=0)$ and Chern-insulating phases $(C= \pm 1)$. Employing the Kubo formalism for the optical conductivity together with the reflection matrix for a substrate-supported conducting sheet, we compute helicity-dependent finite-waist displacements of a reflected Gaussian beam. The resulting optical response exhibits a minimum interband absorption threshold, a Van Hove-type spectral feature, and distinct transitions at the $X$ and $Y$ points arising from the momentum dependence of the exchange field. Under the specified Hall-tensor and polarization sign conventions, the longitudinal helicity half-separation is odd upon reversal of the optical Hall conductivity and correspondingly changes sign between opposite-Chern phases, whereas the transverse half-separation is even in the Hall response. The maximal spin-dependent splitting occur in the vicinity of the pseudo-Brewster reflectance minimum. The longitudinal spin splitting reverses sign between opposite Chern phases, reflecting the exchange-controlled optical Hall response, while its pronounced spectral variations reveal the influence of inequivalent interband transitions induced by the $d$-wave altermagnetic exchange. These findings establish polarization-resolved photonic beam shifts as a sensitive probe of Hall-active topological phases and their characteristic optical spectra.

papers.title: Perception, Not Reasoning, Limits Visual Theory of Mind
papers.authors: Mohamed Rayan Barhdadi; Syed Talal Wasim; Juergen Gall; Erchin Serpedin; Hasan Kurban
papers.abstract: Vision-language models pass text-based false-belief probes at near-human levels but drop by over twenty percentage points on abstract panels the moment the same problem is conveyed visually. The consensus diagnosis is conceptual, prescribing new belief-reasoning modules. We argue the dominant bottleneck is perceptual: not what the model cannot reason about, but what it cannot see. We propose a five-condition dissociation protocol that holds the reasoning task constant while varying perceptual fidelity from visual only to text only, and quantify the result with the Perceptual Contribution Ratio, the share of the visual-to-text gap a given fidelity closes. We test this on two kinds of scenes: abstract 2D panels in the Heider--Simmel tradition, and naturalistic 3D game scenes from MuMA-ToM and MindPower. The evaluation covers seven VLMs and roughly 159,000 API calls. Ground-truth scaffolds substantially close the gap in every setting, and on the abstract panels and MuMA-ToM they match or exceed the text-only reasoning. Whereas scaffolds built by automatic parsers, including frontier VLMs, fail. The most common error in the visual-only condition is \emph{reality bias}, which accounts for 60\% of false-belief failures. Models report where an object actually is, not where an absent agent believes it is. This points to a perceptual front-end that fails to track which agents were present at each moment. Under the evaluated protocol, structured visual scene-state extraction, rather than belief inference, is the dominant bottleneck for visual ToM.

papers.title: From Machine-Discovered Graphs to Analytic NOON State Families
papers.authors: Ozra Mahmoudi; Fatemeh Ahmadi; Rahman Nouroozi
papers.abstract: Machine-discovered graphs generate NOON states after heralding and output-number selection, but their interference mechanisms and optical implementations are not immediately apparent. We derive analytic weight conditions for arbitrary photon number $N$ by counting pair-generation processes that cancel mixed output occupations. These conditions yield quantum experiments by path identity using a Hong-Ou-Mandel interferometer and photon-pair sources. Takagi decomposition of the pair-amplitude matrix gives an exact Gaussian implementation using single-mode squeezers followed by a passive interferometer. Any pure, zero-displacement Gaussian scheme with photon-number-resolved heralding requires at least $N-2$ herald photons, and both constructions attain this bound. At finite gain, the ideal Takagi implementation maintains unit fidelity after output-number selection, whereas fidelity decreases in path identity with fixed source settings.

papers.title: An Information-Theoretic Perspective on Spectral Reconstruction in Lattice QCD
papers.authors: Nan Wang; Long-cheng Gui; Jian Liang; Jun Shi; Han-yang Xing
papers.abstract: Assessing the reliability of spectral reconstruction from finite, noisy lattice correlators requires understanding the constraints supplied by the data relative to prior assumptions. We develop an information-theoretic framework using Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergences to quantify the information supplied by the data through changes from prior to posterior probability distributions. Our analysis accounts for both changes in the probability distributions of spectral strength at individual energies and constraints encoded in correlations across the spectrum. We smear these information measures over neighboring energies using Gaussian weights to obtain a smoothed assessment at a specified energy scale. We demonstrate this framework using a hierarchical Bayesian reconstruction method with posterior sampling, applied to mock correlator data generated from a three-peak spectrum and a near-physical lattice proton correlator. These calculations show that the information measures help explain the properties of reconstructed spectra. They also provide a semiquantitative criterion for assessing how strongly reconstructed spectral structures are constrained by the data and how reliable they are in light of prior effects.

papers.title: A Beltrami Mode in Extreme Fractional Hydrodynamics under Stochastic Forcing
papers.authors: José I. H. López
papers.abstract: We construct an exact stochastic solution of the extreme order endpoint of adaptive fractional Navier Stokes (AFNS) hydrodynamics on the three-dimensional periodic torus. A helical Beltrami eigenfield reduces the nonlinear vector equation to a scalar Ornstein Uhlenbeck process when the white-in-time forcing is aligned with that eigenfield. The resulting invariant Gaussian law yields explicit formulas for the stationary energy, its fluctuations, temporal correlations, circulation, and helicity. Under the same forcing, the corresponding classical Navier Stokes mode has a stationary energy that diverges as the Reynolds number tends to infinity, while the Euler limit exhibits linear growth of the mean energy and has no invariant probability law. The construction isolates, without a cascade hypothesis, the statistical effect of the finite fractional dissipation retained at the extreme endpoint of AFNS.

papers.title: VAComp: View-Aware Full Projector Compensation
papers.authors: Kai Zhou; Qingyue Deng; Bingyao Huang
papers.abstract: Full projector compensation adjusts a projector's input image to compensate for both geometric and photometric distortions introduced by the projection surface. Existing methods generally treat the viewing condition as a static camera viewpoint. When applied to a moving viewer, existing methods face two key challenges: (1) view-dependent methods require model retraining or recalibration to compensate for novel viewpoints; and (2) NeRF/GS-based view-agnostic methods use structure from motion (SfM) to calibrate the projector-camera systems (ProCams) with an unknown global scale, while view-aware tracking requires calibrating a camera oriented opposite to the projector, which introduces an additional calibration challenge. To address these challenges, we introduce VAComp, the first view-aware framework for full projector compensation for a moving viewer in a naked-eye setting. Using a projector, VAComp enables the viewer to perceive a virtual object that visually replaces the real object or to observe view-consistent modifications of the real object's appearance and material properties. To resolve the SfM scale ambiguity, we use metric calibration as a reference to recover the global scale; to calibrate the oppositely facing camera, we use two checkerboards, one facing the RGB camera and the other facing the depth camera. To balance compensation quality and runtime efficiency, we develop two non-iterative hybrid methods, VAComp-SD and VAComp-SI. Both combine 2D Gaussian-based view-conditioned geometric correction with learned photometric compensation, predicting each compensation image through a single forward pass without per-frame iterative optimization. Real-world experiments show that both methods achieve competitive compensation quality, with VAComp-SD enabling real-time updates and VAComp-SI operating at interactive rates. Project page: https://realkaizhou.github.io/VAComp/.

papers.title: Neural Networks with Local Converging Inputs for Solving the 3D Stokes Equations on Unstructured Meshes: Novel Techniques and Advances
papers.authors: Farjana Siddiqua; Haoxiang Huang; Weiming Ding; Haotian Sun; Vigor Yang et al.
papers.abstract: Neural-network surrogates for fluid-flow PDEs usually learn the solution globally, which requires large networks and many high-fidelity training simulations. Neural networks with local converging inputs (NNLCI) instead work locally. They predict the high-fidelity solution at a point from two converging coarse-grid solutions sampled near that point, which keeps the network small, needs little training data, and generalizes across geometries. Here, the two low-fidelity meshes, LF1 and LF2, have on average about 300 and 730 tetrahedra, compared with about 155,000 in the high-fidelity mesh (HF). In this work, we develop an NNLCI framework for three-dimensional Stokes equations on unstructured tetrahedral meshes and introduce two techniques for building local inputs near complex curved boundaries. First, input patches may extend beyond the boundary, with the outside values obtained from a local least-squares fit, so that every high-fidelity point can be predicted, including those next to the wall. Second, the local mesh spacing is estimated from neighboring centroids, which sets the stencil size consistently on unstructured meshes. For pipe flows with one to three bumps, including a circumferentially rotated bump, NNLCI reduces the relative $L^2$ error of the finer low-fidelity solution by $90\%$ to $94\%$, evaluated at all high-fidelity points. Both techniques carry over to other NNLCI problems with smooth solutions on point-cloud discretizations.

papers.title: Remarks on spectral gaps on Gaussian path space
papers.authors: Bo Wu; Zhilai Wen
papers.abstract: In this paper, we discuss the relationship between spectral gaps of Ornstein--Uhlenbeck/$L^2$ operators on Gaussian path space and the underlying Volterra kernel $F$. This framework includes fractional Brownian motion $B^H$ with Hurst index $H\in(0,1)$. For the fractional Wiener measure $μ_H$, the logarithmic Sobolev inequality with respect to the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Dirichlet form holds for $H\geq\frac12$, whereas the corresponding weak Poincaré inequality fails for $0<H<\frac12$. The damped/$L^2$ Dirichlet forms satisfy logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for every $H\in(0,1)$.

papers.title: Agentic discrete-event simulation for manufacturing system design: an open 3D simulator, a benchmark and an industrial case
papers.authors: Javier Pernas-Álvarez; Diego Crespo-Pereira
papers.abstract: The design of manufacturing systems relies on discrete-event simulation (DES) models that experts still build in tool-specific interfaces. AI agents can now write simulation code, but every model they write from scratch is new, unverified software. We present SimuLean, an open-source 3D DES simulator on the Unity engine designed to be programmed by AI agents: its modelling semantics are verified once, in the platform, and the agent builds and studies one model through domain-level commands, in the 3D scene or headless; physically simulated durations are calibrated for fast headless studies. We evaluated it on 18 manufacturing modelling tasks, from single machines to published production lines. A frontier agent built valid models in 93 of 108 attempts (86%), in about two minutes each; on the benchmark's interface version, two frontier agents built 105 of 108 models through domain commands alone, so that each comes with a record of how it was built. Every residual failure was silent - a model that builds and runs but answers wrongly - and only comparison with reference models revealed them all. In an industrial case, one agent working alone rebuilt, verified and studied a robotised welding workshop from a published study, in SimuLean and in SimPy. Comparing them with the published, expert-built model exposed an error in it; against the corrected model, the agent-built models agree within 1%. One agent can already build complete, realistic and traceable models for the design of manufacturing systems; independent reference models are what make them trustworthy.

papers.title: ZARA: Zero-shot Animatable and Relightable 3D Avatar reconstruction from a single image
papers.authors: Yixiao Chen; Dongdong Weng; Chengfeng Zhao; Tao Gong; Zhihe Zhao et al.
papers.abstract: Recent large human reconstruction models create remarkable animatable 3D avatars from a single image, but their appearance remains entangled with the illumination and cannot be relighted. In contrast, existing 3D relightable-avatar reconstruction methods typically require person-specific optimization. We present ZARA, a zero-shot feed-forward framework that reconstructs an animatable 3D Gaussian avatar together with its intrinsic attributes from a single image. ZARA couples a pretrained large-scale human reconstruction model with a Material Transformer to inherit geometry priors while learning material-aware Gaussian representations. To preserve localized details, we introduce Gaussian-aligned material feature fusion strategy, which injects multi-scale material features onto individual Gaussians and combines them with geometry tokens. As most human-avatar datasets lack ground-truth material maps, we use pseudo-material labels as conditioning inputs and supervision targets during training. We further introduce MatFace regularization to preserve facial structure and color in albedo prediction under unreliable facial pseudo-material supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ZARA reconstructs animatable and relightable humans within tens of seconds without person-specific optimization or post-processing, outperforming existing baselines in both relighting quality and materials generalization ability. As the ability of recovering the physically-based-rendering attributes of the human, ZARA also enables direct material editing of the avatar's appearance.

papers.title: HSGNav: Hypothesis Scene Graphs for Multi-Scale Lifelong Navigation under Object Relocation
papers.authors: Kaiyao Liao; Qingfeng Li; Chen Chen; Qing Sun; Ningbo Gu et al.
papers.abstract: In real homes, assistive robots must repeatedly locate targets from large furniture to tiny tabletop items, as people move objects between household surfaces. Uniformly instantiating detections at different scales as 3D objects can be brittle for small on-surface items; without explicit object-state validation, stale entries may persist after scene changes. Our key insight is to separate persistent 3D furniture entities from revisable surface-object hypotheses, retaining their visual evidence without requiring independent object geometry. We formalize this design as the Hypothesis Scene Graph (HSG), which preserves small-object evidence and supports local revision without rebuilding the stable entity topology. Building on HSG, HSGNav uses this separation for multi-scale lifelong navigation: retrieval selects entity or hypothesis evidence according to target scale, exploration acquires additional surface observations, and verification confirms target presence or invalidates contradicted hypothesis records. Because existing lifelong benchmarks such as GOAT-Bench rarely require mid-episode memory invalidation or multi-scale search, we introduce FAROS-Bench (Find And Re-find Objects across Scales) for mid-episode relocation of surface objects and multi-scale find goals. Experiments show that HSGNav performs competitively on GOAT-Bench while substantially outperforming prior methods on FAROS-Bench.

papers.title: Scaling Optimization-Oriented Hypernetworks for Implicit Neural Representations
papers.authors: Lulu Cai; Hanxiang Ren; Siyan Dong; Li Sun; Jiefeng Wu et al.
papers.abstract: We present a hypernetwork that generates the parameters of an implicit neural representation (INR) for a given signal in a single forward pass, without test-time optimization. Existing hypernetworks for this problem either ignore the chain-rule structure of the test-time optimization that produces an INR or, when they preserve it, instantiate the structure with MLPs whose parameter count grows quartically in target-network width. Our central contribution is to show that this parameter-count cost is structural to the MLP instantiation, not to the optimization-oriented principle of preserving chain-rule structure, and to resolve it by replacing the MLP body with attention. The resulting hypernetwork combines three design choices: an output-neuron-centric tokenization that aligns the token axis with each layer's output-neuron axis; an information-flow consistency rule that fixes the role of every cross-attention module from the representation its output should occupy; and a token-space iterative rollout that realizes the five quantities one optimization step on the target INR computes as five cross-attention modules with parameter count independent of target-network width. Across five 2D and 3D INR generation benchmarks, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art single-pass and optimization-oriented baselines; scales to target-network widths at which the MLP-based optimization-oriented paradigm exhausts GPU memory; and produces the highest result on NeRF generation without ground-truth INR weights supervision.

papers.title: They Can See It but Not Say It: Iterative Self Knowledge Re-expression in Visual Reasoning Relative Pose Identification
papers.authors: Mengyu Wang; Ken Deng; Yftah Ziser; Shay B. Cohen; Tiejun Ma
papers.abstract: The task of visual reasoning relative pose identification (VRRPI) has exposed critical weaknesses in the multi-view 3D spatial reasoning capabilities of modern vision-language models (VLMs). We present a systematic analysis of VLMs' behavior in VRRPI, uncovering stable output biases where VLMs disproportionately predict specific motion patterns regardless of visual evidence. To mitigate these inherent biases, we propose self knowledge re-expression with iterative debiasing (SKR-ID), an annotation-free pipeline that adapts VLMs for VRRPI using only randomly extracted unannotated image pairs. SKR-ID transitions VLMs' output mechanism from generic next-token prediction to task-optimized classification heads. The pipeline proceeds in two stages: (1) a cold-start initialization using debiasing object-centric prompts to anchor motion inference in 2D visual evidence; and (2) a recursive logit-ranking mechanism that enforces statistical parity by using the median logit value as a dynamic threshold. Experimental evaluation across frontier VLMs on standard benchmarks demonstrates that SKR-ID significantly mitigates systematic biases. Our method improves open-source VLMs' Macro-F1 scores from 35.0-45.4% to 53.7-58.0%, without using any annotated data. These results show that SKR-ID can effectively improve 3D reasoning performance from a severely collapsed baseline. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/astudentuser/Codes_of_SKR-ID.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Langevin Dynamics for Stochastic Nonconvex Optimization: Curvature Regularization and Non-Asymptotic Guarantees
papers.authors: Stefano Bruno; Dong-Young Lim
papers.abstract: Zeroth-order methods provide a way to optimize stochastic nonconvex objectives using only noisy function evaluations. However, the smoothing inherent in their gradient estimators effectively modifies the objective being optimized. In particular, Gaussian smoothing with smoothing parameter $η>0$ induces, to leading order, an implicit Hessian-trace regularization, which motivates the study of the curvature-regularized objective of the form $f(x)+(η^2/2) tr(\nabla^2 f(x))$. We develop a non-asymptotic theory in the nonconvex setting for a class of algorithms called stochastic zeroth-order Langevin dynamics (ZOLD), which use only noisy function evaluations and do not have access to first- or higher-order derivative information, and derive excess-risk guarantees for the curvature-regularized objective. We first control the finite-time distribution of the ZOLD iterates in Wasserstein distance with respect to the Gibbs measure associated with the Gaussian-smoothed objective. An explicit coupling between the smoothing and inverse temperature parameters then quantifies the proximity of this measure to the Gibbs measure associated with the corresponding Hessian-trace-regularized objective. These distributional estimates in Wasserstein distance lead to excess-risk bounds for the curvature-regularized objective. Our analysis accommodates assumptions under which the stochastic function evaluations are allowed to have non-uniform dependence on the data stream. In addition, the constants in the non-asymptotic bounds do not rely on log-Sobolev or Poincaré inequalities as in prior zeroth-order Langevin analyses. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first non-asymptotic analysis of a zeroth-order Langevin method that simultaneously establishes excess-risk guarantees for a curvature-regularized objective and Wasserstein guarantees for the associated Gibbs measure in the nonconvex setting.

papers.title: HINSPHERES: Spherically Symmetric Radiative Transfer Modeling of HINSA and the Radial HI-to-H$_2$ Transition in Molecular Clouds
papers.authors: Yuchen Xing; Di Li; Xin Lyu; Pei Zuo; Yulian Guo et al.
papers.abstract: The transition from atomic hydrogen (HI) to molecular hydrogen (H$_2$) is the first step in the evolution from diffuse interstellar gas to dense star-forming cores. HI narrow self-absorption (HINSA), produced by cold atomic gas mixed with molecular material, provides a direct tracer of the HI-to-H$_2$ transition in molecular clouds. Existing HINSA analyses typically model HINSA as a single Gaussian component with a uniform spin temperature. This approach cannot recover the radial HI distribution and yields large errors for young cores whose profiles deviate from a Gaussian shape. Here we present hinspheres, an open-source framework that models the core as onion-like spherically symmetric concentric shells, solves radiative transfer along the line of sight and jointly fits the HI abundance, temperature, and kinematic parameters. The framework recovers all parameters with a mean relative error of 4.6-6.8% on our synthetic data with different ages. A combined resolution-noise grid shows that the median recovery error remains below 16% for cores within 1 kpc observed at FAST resolution with noise levels below 0.2 K. Applying it to the dark cores L1574 and L1544, we reveal radial HI abundance profiles that span about three orders of magnitude, which were missed by the single-Gaussian method. The derived chemical ages are $6.5\times10^6$ and $8.7\times10^6$ yr, respectively. Compared with the commonly used single-Gaussian method, hinspheres characterizes the radial profile of HINSA structures more accurately, making it well suited to identifying and analyzing young cores undergoing the HI-to-H$_2$ transition.

papers.title: Bayesian Low-Rank Posteriors for Scalable Membership Inference
papers.authors: Khanh Nguyen; Antonio Emanuele Cinà; Andrey Barsky; Alejandra Reinares; Fabio Roli et al.
papers.abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIAs) aim to determine whether a sample was used during the training of a target model. Strong MIAs rely on reference (or shadow) models to estimate target-conditional score distributions, but training such ensembles is computationally expensive for modern large-scale Vision--Language Models (VLMs). In this work, we propose a scalable alternative that replaces explicit reference-model training with a Bayesian approximation over low-rank adaptation parameters. Specifically, we model uncertainty only within the LoRA subspace and construct a posterior from a single training run, from which we sample a diverse set of \emph{virtual reference models}. We instantiate this approach using Stochastic Weight Averaging Gaussian (SWAG), enabling efficient approximation of target-conditional score distributions at a fraction of the cost of conventional shadow-model ensembles. We evaluate the resulting attack on three downstream-adapted VLMs across two privacy-sensitive visual question answering tasks, namely Document VQA and Medical VQA. To isolate the effect of pretraining knowledge, we additionally introduce a controlled synthetic dataset. Our approach outperforms standard reference-based attacks while requiring only a single reference-model fine-tuning run, making membership inference more practical for large VLMs.

papers.title: Spatial Representation Distillation and Knowledge Routing for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Jungin Park; Chaoran Zhu; Changjae Oh; Kwanghoon Sohn
papers.abstract: Understanding three-dimensional physical structure has become essential for vision-language-action models (VLAs). However, existing approaches either rely on explicit geometric inputs at inference time or adopt a single visual pathway, potentially compromising the visual-semantic knowledge inherited from pre-trained models. We present SPARK-VLA, Spatial Representation distillation and Knowledge routing for VLAs, a preserve-specialize-route framework for spatially adapting VLAs without requiring external 3D inputs or experts at inference. SPARK-VLA consists of two key components: (1) spatial representation distillation, which transfers 3D understanding from a frozen 3D expert to a LoRA-adapted visual branch by aligning attention responses while preserving the original visual pathway, and (2) a lightweight knowledge router, which selectively forwards action-relevant visual tokens to the language model using routing supervision derived from action-loss gradients. Across LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, CALVIN, and real-world manipulation, SPARK-VLA achieves strong performance with only a 0.5B language backbone and approximately 53M trainable parameters, providing an effective and parameter-efficient approach to 3D-aware VLA learning. Code is available at https://github.com/park-jungin/spark-vla.

papers.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
papers.authors: Jayan Mukherjee; with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.

papers.title: S2HAND: Accuracy-Preservation Trade-Offs for Hand Specialization in Whole-Body Pose Models
papers.authors: Singyu Muk; Xuanren Song; Kalin Stefanov
papers.abstract: Unified whole-body pose estimators jointly predict body, face, and hand landmarks, but often degrade on small, blurred, or occluded hands. Attaching a standalone hand specialist introduces extra detection overhead, coordinate alignment, and wrist-stitching artifacts. We introduce S2HAND, a hand-specialized Sapiens2-5B framework that preserves the native 308-keypoint output interface. Specifically, S2HAND-MT adapts a lightweight 0.87M-parameter pose branch to route 40 finger heatmaps while strictly preserving the shared Transformer, auxiliary task heads, and the other 268 body, foot, and face heatmaps. S2HAND-Pose further fine-tunes three Fisher-selected Transformer blocks (267.13M parameters), trading exact preservation for stronger hand recovery: it lifts macro AUC from 57.83% to 65.73% across HInt TEST, COCO WholeBody VAL, and FreiHAND EVAL, and surpasses HInt-adapted Hand5/HRNet and stitched Hand5 systems on all five Native Pipeline benchmarks. On COCO, S2HAND-Pose improves hand AP by 12.89 points and body-plus-foot AP by 0.19 points. Across a 512-image multi-task audit, it maintains 99.60% foreground segmentation agreement with the public checkpoint, with quantified normal and pointmap drift. Its 2D coordinates also lower 3D mesh error in frozen Pose2Mesh transfer, while our optional TailGuard re-cropping module cuts S2HAND-MT's severe failure rate on NewDays from 13.45% to 10.43%. S2HAND thus resolves the whole-body hand bottleneck with either exact non-hand preservation (MT) or empirically audited trade-offs (Pose).

papers.title: Tiresias: Towards Language-Conditioned World Models
papers.authors: Fengyi Wu; Yifei Dong; Yetong Sha; Lingdong Kong; Qiyu Hu et al.
papers.abstract: World models enable planning through internal simulation, while natural language provides intuitive task specification. Yet, language-conditioned world modeling remains fragmented across domains with disparate action spaces, datasets, and evaluation protocols. We introduce LCWM, a shared task that maps an initial agent-view observation and a language instruction to an action sequence that fulfills the instruction. Its accompanying benchmark, LCWM-Bench, integrates 15 datasets across navigation, robotics, 3D gaming, and driving under a shared action interface and evaluation protocol, pairing 142,987 episodes with 428,961 instructions in three styles. We further propose Tiresias, an agent that plans via selective imagination: a language-conditioned diffusion policy generates candidate trajectories, a trajectory ranker shortlists them, and a video-pretrained world model imagines their visual consequences. A visual ranker evaluates these rollouts, complementing trajectory scores to select the final plan. Tiresias achieves competitive planning and imagination performance on LCWM-Bench. Ablations demonstrate the complementary benefits of trajectory ranking and visual verification, while experiments with alternative proposal methods show that the trained rankers remain effective beyond our diffusion policy. Together, LCWM-Bench and Tiresias provide a unified evaluation setting and an effective starting point for studying language-guided planning through world models.

papers.title: Quantitative Assessment of Crystal Structure Prediction
papers.authors: Sergio Rincón; Gabriel González; Nicolás Andrade; Rafael Velásquez; Sebastián Ojeda et al.
papers.abstract: Crystal Structure Prediction (CSP) aims to predict a material's 3D structure from its chemical composition, with applications from energy storage to biomedical devices. Despite its importance, existing evaluation frameworks suffer from key limitations: they rely on threshold-sensitive or incomparable metrics, focus predominantly on geometric performance while overlooking physical plausibility, and fail to account for polymorphism, where a chemical composition can crystallize into multiple stable structures. In parallel, recent Symmetry-Informed CSP (SICSP) methods often report results alongside standard CSP baselines while receiving crystallographic templates at inference, which constrain the search space and make SICSP a fundamentally different task. To address these limitations, we introduce an Orientation-invariant, Polymorph-Aware, Large Benchmark (OPAL-Bench) that evaluates CSP and SICSP as separate tasks. We evaluate 7 CSP and 2 SICSP methods under OPAL-Bench across 4 datasets using threshold-free geometric and physical distance metrics. Our results show that no method dominates across all metrics, and that geometric performance is not strongly correlated with physical plausibility. We also release OPAL-CSP, an SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching baseline for the CSP track that performs competitively on geometric metrics and ranks among the best on physical ones. By unifying geometric and physical metrics under a polymorph-aware protocol, OPAL-Bench enables a more comprehensive assessment of generative quality in CSP.

papers.title: RefineSplat: Reconstruction-Guided Object-Centric Gaussian Splatting for Open-Vocabulary Querying
papers.authors: Yiren Lu; Disheng Liu; Sreya Srinidhi; Yunlai Zhou; Yiran Qiao et al.
papers.abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding aims to segment and retrieve arbitrary objects in 3D scenes using natural language queries. Most existing methods typically follow a splat-then-segment paradigm, where 3D Gaussian Splatting is first reconstructed and then augmented with labels or language features for subsequent segmentation. However, this pipeline often suffers from view inconsistency, ambiguous object boundaries, and weak object-level correspondence, especially in complex static and dynamic scenes. Building on our prior Segment-then-Splat framework, we present RefineSplat, a reconstruction-guided extension that retains its object-centric paradigm: it first tracks objects in 2D and then reconstructs each object with a dedicated set of 3D Gaussians, preserving explicit object-Gaussian correspondence for unified open-vocabulary segmentation and retrieval. To improve robustness, we further close the loop between 2D tracking and 3D reconstruction. Since off-the-shelf video trackers can produce unreliable masks that propagate errors into object reconstruction, we introduce a reconstruction-guided feedback mechanism that refines object tracking using rendered masks and multi-view consistency. Moreover, instead of assigning each object a single language embedding, we propose a viewpoint-aware embedding assignment strategy, where each object maintains multiple view-clustered embeddings to capture view-dependent semantic cues. We also introduce Blender-OVS, a synthetic benchmark of static and dynamic sequences with exact object meshes and point clouds, enabling direct evaluation of extracted geometry. Experiments on static and dynamic benchmarks show improved rendered-view segmentation and lower object-level Chamfer distances, with competitive scene reconstruction quality.

papers.title: SAMBoost: Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting
papers.authors: Mulah Moriah; Franck Vermet; Pierre Ailliot; Juliette Legrand
papers.abstract: We propose SAMBoost (Spatially Aware Mesh Boosting), a gradient boosting method that combines tree-based covariate modelling with a stochastic partial differential equation (SPDE) latent spatial field through a single penalised objective. At each boosting iteration, the predictor is decomposed into separate covariate and spatial components. The method is motivated by applications in which the spatial effect is not a nuisance to be removed but a quantity of interest that must be recovered alongside the covariates. In insurance, for example, practitioners need both flexible nonlinear covariate effects and an interpretable geographic risk surface that can be reported on its own. Existing approaches often involve trade-offs, offering flexible covariate modelling but no explicit spatial field, rigorous spatial inference with a fixed additive covariate structure, or a combination of both at computational costs that limit practicality for large datasets. SAMBoost addresses these goals within the boosting loop, and the underlying mesh produces a sparse precision structure whose cost is largely independent of sample size. On simulations and on an open benchmark, SAMBoost matches or improves on the predictive accuracy of joint Gaussian process and tree boosting approaches. It is also faster and recovers the spatial field and covariate effects more accurately. When covariate effects include interactions, it outperforms additive Bayesian spatial models. Applied to a flood insurance portfolio with 4.9 million records, SAMBoost trains on the full training set without subsampling and runs about sixteen times faster than a Bayesian reference, with a consistent spatial risk surface. A public Python implementation is available.

papers.title: ClearForm: Shared-Surface Gaussian Splatting for Transparent and Opaque Scenes
papers.authors: Hajeong Lee; Jong-Il Park
papers.abstract: Transparent-interface reconstruction must recover glass surfaces even when most observed color comes from the scene behind them. We present ClearForm, a shared-planar-Gaussian method for jointly reconstructing transparent interfaces and the appearance seen through them. We identify and analyze the Geometry-Appearance Compositing Dilemma (GACD): when the same transparency-dependent alpha controls both color and geometry, revealing the background can weaken a transparent surface's contribution to geometric reconstruction. We derive its effect on plane-based depth estimation, identify a mechanism that can weaken geometric learning, and quantify the loss of interface support through controlled comparisons. To address this conflict, we develop geometry-preserving dual-opacity surface reconstruction. Shared planar Gaussians retain interface contributions in geometry compositing while modeling transmission and sparse reflection in RGB, supported by transparency-aware geometric constraints. To manage the different primitive-visibility requirements of these compositors, we introduce Dual-Evidence Lifecycle (DEL), which retains Gaussians supported by multi-view geometry or RGB reconstruction evidence. On 3D-FRONT-T, ClearForm achieves 27.05 mm Chamfer distance (CD) and 0.928 F1, compared with 59.18 mm CD for our PGSR reproduction and the reported 34 mm CD and 0.836 F1 for GLINT. On TransLab, it achieves 1.65 mm CD, 0.963 F1, and 40.14 dB PSNR. In matched ablations, dual-opacity compositing reduces CD from 59.25 to 27.09 mm, while DEL improves PSNR by 2.06 dB. Our project page is available at https://hajeongx.github.io/clearform/.

papers.title: Telling coordination from coincidence: a no-interaction twin for collective systems
papers.authors: Eric J. Couture
papers.abstract: Measures of emergence based on information theory or causal closure ask whether a group variable has a predictable law of its own, but not whether that law was produced by the members' interactions: the centre of mass of non-interacting random walkers passes the standard criterion $Ψ$. We introduce the interaction share S, the fraction of the forecast error of a system's no-interaction twin (the same members with every interaction removed) that the real group law eliminates, and a projected estimator with expectation zero without interaction. For Gaussian forecasts, $-\frac{1}{2}\ln(1-S)$ is the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence of the real group law from the twin's. S is exactly zero for the centre of mass of linearly coupled walkers, and a machine-checked proof extends this to any pairwise force obeying Newton's third law. Across magnets, oscillators and flocking models it rises from 0 to about 1 where collective order appears. With time-shifted virtual groups and positive controls, it separates real fish schools (0.54-0.91, 17 recordings, two species) from groups that never interacted (-0.10 to 0.07), and it falls to zero when zebrafish are placed in the dark. In 221 mouse brain areas and in US stock markets the shares are small (about 1-3%) and were confirmed in pre-registered tests on unseen data. For linear forecasts the share is a memory gap, computable from two autocorrelation curves without fitting a twin; it matches measured shares (Spearman 0.97) and predicted fresh markets within 0.004. All code, data pipelines and hashed pre-registrations are public.

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Generalization for Set-Input Optimization-Valued Objectives
papers.authors: Futoshi Futami; Masahiro Fujisawa
papers.abstract: Modern machine learning is increasingly evaluated using criteria such as multicalibration, CVaR, and Cressie-Read DRO, which target subgroup reliability, tail risk, and distributional robustness rather than averages of fixed per-example losses. Existing information-theoretic generalization bounds for pointwise losses do not directly apply, because these empirical criteria depend on the entire batch and involve a post-hoc auxiliary optimization over witnesses, thresholds, or reweightings. We formalize this structure as set-input optimization-valued objectives. In the balanced supersample setting, we bound the expected optimized validation-training gap in terms of an objective-dependent sub-Gaussian parameter and the square root of the prediction-based conditional mutual information (fCMI) between the learned supersample prediction table and the selector vector. Combining this with fixed-predictor population-validation comparisons yields unified algorithm-dependent generalization bounds. We verify sub-Gaussianity of the selector gap using stability and convex L2-Lipschitz certificates, obtaining concrete bounds for multicalibration, CVaR, and Cressie-Read DRO, with a stability-based single-index refinement.

papers.title: MambaLoc: Lightweight Indoor Localization Using Cross-Modal Knowledge Distillation
papers.authors: Mohab Bahnassy; Omar Saqr; Hamada Rizk; Moustafa Youssef
papers.abstract: Accurate indoor localization on resource-constrained edge devices remains challenging due to the tension between modeling fidelity and computational efficiency. Wi-Fi Channel State Information (CSI) enables low-cost deployment using existing Wi-Fi infrastructure but is heavily distorted by multipath propagation. Transformer-based solutions mitigate these effects but their quadratic complexity limits real-time edge deployment. Ultra-Wideband (UWB) provides geometrically precise ranging yet requires dedicated infrastructure. We present MambaLoc, a cross-modal distillation framework that improves the accuracy-efficiency balance in CSI-based localization. MambaLoc uses a linear-time Selective State Space Model (Mamba) as a lightweight CSI student, guided during training by a UWB-Transformer teacher. A Feature Alignment Module bridges the representational gap between heterogeneous RF modalities, allowing the CSI model to inherit UWB-derived geometric structure without UWB hardware at inference. A probabilistic Gaussian Mixture regression head models multi-modal spatial ambiguity from multipath effects, avoiding the physically implausible averaging of deterministic regression. Evaluations on a real-world dataset show MambaLoc achieves a median localization error of 0.230 m, reducing error by 22.2% over a standalone Mamba baseline, while requiring 65.1% fewer FLOPs and 58% lower inference latency than Transformer-based approaches.
